interrogator_dossier:
# Forensic Dossier — Seres Group Co., Ltd. (9927.HK, H-shares)

**Prepared as of 2026-07-17. Live price HK$42.08 (prior close HK$45.22 — the figure carried in the screener scan). Fundamentals reported in Chinese yuan (RMB); the quote is in Hong Kong dollars (HKD). Conversion used: 1 RMB ≈ 1.09 HKD.**

> **Identity correction — read first.** The screener scan left the company name blank, and the peer-comps file for this ticker names it "Zhejiang Leapmotor." That is wrong. Ticker 9927 on the Hong Kong exchange is **Seres Group Co., Ltd. — H shares** (the Huawei-partnered maker of the AITO / Wenjie premium electric vehicles; A-shares trade in Shanghai as 601127). Leapmotor is a different company (9863.HK). Every hard number in the scan matches Seres, not Leapmotor: 2024 revenue of RMB 145.2 billion, first-ever annual profit of RMB 5.95 billion, and the jump from RMB 35.8 billion of revenue in 2023 are Seres's figures exactly — Leapmotor did roughly RMB 32 billion of revenue in 2024. The rest of this dossier treats the name as Seres.

> **Evidence note.** No earnings-call transcript was bundled, and our licensed transcript feed is not subscribed for this name. This dossier therefore cross-references management's *public* statements — the July 13, 2026 profit warning, the April 30, 2026 first-quarter release, and the November 2025 listing prospectus — against the hard financials in the scan. No quotes are invented; where I could not source a claim I say so.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Seres is one of the most violent boom-and-bust stories in the China electric-vehicle complex. For most of its life (as Chongqing Sokon) it was a loss-making minivan and small-car maker. The story changed completely when it became Huawei's flagship manufacturing partner for the AITO ("Wenjie") brand — premium, Huawei-software-defined SUVs. The AITO M9, a vehicle priced above RMB 500,000, became the best-selling model in its class in China through 2024. That drove the revenue explosion visible in the scan: from RMB 35.8 billion (2023) to RMB 145.2 billion (2024) to RMB 165.1 billion (2025), and the first profits in the company's history (RMB 5.95 billion in 2024, RMB 5.96 billion in 2025).

The company then did two things that define today's setup. First, in November 2025 it listed H-shares in Hong Kong at HK$131.50, raising about HK$14.3 billion — the largest carmaker listing in Hong Kong in four years, with roughly US$8.3 billion of cornerstone demand. Second, it bought a 10% stake in Huawei's smart-car unit, Shenzhen Yinwang Intelligent Technology, for RMB 11.5 billion, and acquired the AITO trademark from Huawei for about RMB 2.5 billion — an attempt to own more of the value chain rather than rent all of it.

The arc has since inverted hard. The stock is down about 61% this year and roughly 68% from its November listing price, and management on July 13, 2026 warned of a first-half loss. The narrative has flipped from "Huawei's profit engine" to "sells more, loses more."

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management's claim / public position | What the financials show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Premium franchise with real pricing power (AITO as "China's #1 luxury NEV brand," per its own Brand Finance citation) | 2024–25 net margin was thin for a "premium" maker — 3.6% net in 2025 — and it *collapsed into a loss* in Q2 2026 the moment input costs rose. Gross margin 29.1% in 2025 but not defended. | Poorer than the story — the margin is fragile, not premium-durable |
| Growth is intact (Q1 2026 revenue +34.5% to RMB 25.75bn; NEV unit sales +43.9%) | True for Q1, but H1 total vehicles fell ~1% YoY to 196,580 and **June sales fell 28.1% YoY**. Momentum reversed within the half. | Matched early, then broke |
| "Ample cash reserves and a sound balance-sheet structure" (July 13 warning) | Verified: net cash of about RMB 59.75bn (cash RMB 64.13bn vs total debt RMB 4.38bn) at March 31, 2026. This is the strongest part of the story. | Verified |
| The half-year loss is a cost shock, not a demand problem | H1 2026 loss of RMB 1.5–1.8bn (vs +RMB 2.94bn a year earlier) is blamed on memory-chip prices up ~5x, lithium carbonate up ~125%, and asset write-downs. But June volume −28% says demand also softened. | Partly true — cost is the headline, but demand is cracking too |
| Capital allocation is building an ecosystem asset (Yinwang stake, AITO trademark) | Real cash out the door — RMB 11.5bn for 10% of Yinwang, ~RMB 2.5bn for the trademark. Strategic, but it consumed a large slice of the cash the balance-sheet story rests on. | Real, but reduces the "free" cash |

The core tension: the revenue and the 2024–25 profit turn are genuine, but the profitability proved to be a **thin, cost-sensitive spread on a Huawei-defined product** rather than a durable premium margin. The first serious input-cost shock erased two years of margin progress in a single quarter.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining.** Without call transcripts I read tone from the cadence of disclosures. The November 2025 prospectus and the April 2026 Q1 release were offensive in posture — record IPO, new-model launches (the all-new M9 pre-sale, the M6 with "10,000 orders in 15 minutes"), overseas-expansion spend. By the July 13, 2026 warning the language turned defensive and balance-sheet-first ("ample cash reserves," "sound balance-sheet structure," "short-term profitability impacted by rising raw-material costs"). The shift from talking about growth and orders to reassuring on solvency is the classic offensive-to-defensive rotation.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Low-to-Medium, and freshly damaged.** The company does not give tight numeric guidance in the Western sense, so I judge credibility by the gap between the confident Q1 framing (revenue +34%, sales +44%) and the H1 outcome (a loss and a ~1% volume decline for the half). A company that reported a RMB 754 million Q1 profit on April 30 pre-announced a first-half *loss* ten weeks later — meaning Q2 was catastrophic (the AITO subsidiary alone lost RMB 1.9–2.15bn in the quarter). The speed of that reversal is the single most credibility-damaging fact here. The one claim I can independently corroborate — the strong net-cash position — is verified, which is why credibility is not lower than it is.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

The pressure points the market is pressing on, and where management has been thin:
- **Structural margin.** Is Seres a premium brand or a contract assembler for Huawei that keeps a thin slice? The Q2 loss argues the latter. Management has not credibly answered this.
- **Huawei dependence and value capture.** Huawei now spreads the same smart-car technology across a stable of partners (Avatr, Luxeed with Chery, Stelato with BAIC, Maextro with JAC). Each new sibling brand dilutes AITO's exclusivity and Huawei's incentive to favor Seres. Management frames the Yinwang stake as alignment; skeptics read it as paying Huawei for a seat it cannot afford to lose.
- **The cash question.** How much of the RMB 59.75bn net cash is genuinely free versus working-capital float owed to suppliers, plus the remaining Yinwang installment and the R&D spend the IPO earmarked (70% of proceeds)? Management leads with the gross figure and does not bridge to distributable cash.
- **Citi (analyst Jeff Chung)** cut the A-share target to RMB 37.40 from RMB 55.40 in July 2026 and kept a Sell rating — the street is not giving the recovery the benefit of the doubt.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 A Q1 profit (RMB 754m) flipping to a pre-announced H1 loss (−RMB 1.5–1.8bn) within ten weeks — margin has no shock absorber.
🔴 June 2026 unit sales −28.1% YoY — the demand side is weakening at the same time as costs, not just costs alone.
🔴 Asset write-downs for models/assets "limited by technological iteration" — an admission that recent capital spending is aging faster than expected in a brutal product cycle.
🔴 Rented moat: the brand's appeal and the intelligent-driving stack belong substantially to Huawei, which is actively multiplying its OEM partners.
🔴 Stock down nine consecutive months; H-share IPO buyers (Nov 2025, HK$131.50) are down ~68% — a demoralized, potentially forced shareholder base.
🟢 Genuine net cash of ~RMB 59.75bn against a market value of roughly RMB 63–70bn — the balance sheet is a real cushion, unusual for a China EV maker.
🟢 A strategic 10% Yinwang stake (RMB 11.5bn at cost) and the owned AITO trademark — real assets with option value if Yinwang ever lists.
🟢 The cost drivers (memory, lithium) are cyclical commodity/component prices that can normalize; the loss is not (yet) a demand-collapse story alone.
🟢 AITO deliveries still grew modestly in H1 (NEV units +3.9%), so the franchise has not lost the customer outright.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The pivot in disclosure language from "orders and launches" to "balance-sheet resilience" is the tell that management expects a rough few quarters, not a one-print blip.
- Buying the trademark and a Yinwang stake *before* the downturn hit suggests management sensed its dependence on Huawei was a strategic vulnerability — the "Seres can no longer rely solely on Huawei" theme in the Chinese press predates the crash.
- The H-share now trades near, and arguably below, the level Citi assigns the A-share (RMB 37.40) — for a dual-listed name where the A-share usually trades at a *premium*, the H-line is priced for something close to the bear case already.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: DETERIORATING.** The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: this is a genuinely cheap balance sheet wrapped around an earnings engine whose durability was just disproven. The net cash and the Yinwang stake are real and large relative to the market value — on an enterprise-value basis (market value minus net cash) the market is paying almost nothing for the auto business plus the Yinwang stake. That is the entire bull case. Against it: there is no dated catalyst forcing a re-rating, the operating trend is still worsening (June volume −28%, Q2 subsidiary loss ~RMB 2bn), and the margin proved to be a thin, cost-sensitive spread on a product Seres does not fully own.

**Moat:** narrow and eroding. The AITO franchise is real but substantially *rented* from Huawei, whose expanding partner roster and control of the software/brand economics cap Seres's structural margin — a high-2024/25-margin that fell to a loss on the first cost shock is an eroding position, not a durable one. **Moat trend: eroding.** **Secular threat: material (not terminal)** — the structural risk is Huawei-ecosystem value capture plus the China NEV price war compressing the whole cohort, which impairs the *level* of Seres's terminal margin without extinguishing the franchise. None of the house's named secular-decline themes fits cleanly; this is an intra-industry margin-capture and price-war risk. The cheapness is therefore a genuine fear-print on the assets, but sitting on an earnings base whose normalized power is now unproven — closer to a "cheap on assets, unproven on earnings" situation than a clean mispricing.

CREDIBILITY_SCORE: 3 | TRAJECTORY: DETERIORATING | MOAT: ERODING | MOAT_TREND: ERODING | SECULAR_THREAT: material

bull_thesis: Seres is the maker of the Huawei-partnered AITO (Wenjie) premium electric-vehicle brand, and the bull case is a cash-backed franchise trading near its lows. Three planks support it. First, the balance sheet: as of 31 March 2026 the company held about RMB 64.1B of cash against only RMB 4.4B of debt, or roughly RMB 59.5B net cash. Against a Hong Kong market value of about RMB 76B (1.74B shares at HK$47.8, converted at roughly 1.10 Hong Kong dollars per yuan), net cash alone is worth about HK$37-38 per share -- close to four-fifths of the quote. On top of the cash sits a roughly 10% stake in Huawei's smart-car unit (Yinwang), carried near RMB 13.4B. Strip both out and the market is paying only a low-single-digit multiple for a business that did RMB 165B of revenue and RMB 5.96B of profit in 2025. Second, the franchise is still growing where it counts: AITO deliveries rose about +10% in the first half of 2026 into a weak market, and the new-generation M9 flagship (on sale 27 May 2026 at RMB 479,800) drew more than 10,000 orders within three weeks -- evidence the premium brand still commands demand. Third, the current loss is explicitly attributed to pass-through cost shocks (memory chips, lithium carbonate) and one-off impairments on obsoleted tooling, not to collapsing demand; management and sell-side expect scale economics from the new model cycle to restore profitability in the second half. If margins normalise back toward even the 3-4% net level of 2025 and the cash is partly returned, the shares re-rate toward net cash plus a modest earnings multiple -- roughly HK$60-65. Conditions that must hold: the second-half 2026 margin recovery actually arrives; the payables-funded cash cushion does not drain; and Huawei does not hollow out AITO's position by favouring its newer partners.
bear_thesis: The bear case is that the deep-value screen is measuring a peak that has already passed, and that the cash cushion is softer than it looks. The earnings path is the tell: attributable profit fell from RMB 2.37B in the third quarter of 2025 to RMB 0.64B in the fourth, RMB 0.75B in the first quarter of 2026, and then the company pre-announced (12-13 July 2026) a first-half 2026 loss of RMB 1.5-1.8B versus a RMB 2.94B profit a year earlier. The core AITO brand is the driver, with a second-quarter standalone loss of roughly RMB 2.25-2.55B and a per-vehicle loss above RMB 20,000. The cause is structural, not seasonal: in China's electric-vehicle price war Seres cannot pass rising input costs to buyers, so the margin is the shock absorber, and accelerating model obsolescence forces impairments -- the capital intensity of staying premium is rising faster than the pricing power to fund it. The moat is eroding in plain sight: the Huawei relationship that built AITO is no longer exclusive, with the same technology stack now powering rivals Luxeed (Chery), Stelato (BAIC) and Maextro (JAC). On the balance sheet, the RMB 59.5B net cash sits against RMB 66B of payables on roughly 187-day terms; net cash exceeds total shareholders' equity, which is only possible because supplier float, not shareholder capital, funds it -- and that float unwinds if volumes and the payables cycle reverse. Finally, the Hong Kong line is a tiny (~6%) public float that fell from its HK$131.50 float price (5 November 2025) to the low-HK$40s, and there is no dated, binding catalyst to force a re-rating. What confirms the bear: a second consecutive loss-making quarter, further AITO share loss to Huawei's other partners, or a drawdown in the cash balance as float reverses.
consensus_delta: For a deep-value name the question is whether the street is pricing terminal decline into stable earnings power -- here it is closer to the reverse. The screener and the residual bull anchor still carry a ~RMB 6B annual-profit figure (2025) and a low trailing multiple, treating the near-52-week-low price as a mispricing of a growing premium franchise. The hard record disagrees: attributable profit fell every quarter from RMB 2.37B (Q3 2025) to a first-half 2026 LOSS of RMB 1.5-1.8B, with core AITO losing over RMB 20,000 per vehicle in the second quarter. Where we do disagree with a naive bear is on the cash: about RMB 59.5B net cash and a ~RMB 13.4B Yinwang stake are real and put a genuine floor under the equity -- but where we disagree with the bull is that a large slice of that cash is supplier float (RMB 66B payables at ~187 days; net cash exceeds total equity), so it is not all distributable. Net: the market is roughly right, not badly wrong -- the cheapness on trailing earnings is a peak artifact now that earnings have gone negative.
forcing_function: There is no hard, dated, binding forcing function. The realistic re-rating triggers are soft: (1) H1 2026 results in late August 2026 and Q3 results around October 2026 -- the first evidence of whether the second-half margin recovery is real; (2) monthly AITO delivery prints showing the new M9/M8 cycle restoring scale; (3) any capital-return announcement that converts the cash pile into shareholder value. None is contractual or guaranteed.
valley_of_death: The near-term risk is that the loss is not a one-quarter event. The 12-13 July 2026 warning covers only the first half; the second-quarter AITO loss (RMB 2.25-2.55B standalone) is accelerating, and the three uncertainties management itself flagged -- raw-material price volatility (memory chips, lithium carbonate), an escalating price war, and slower-than-expected new-model ramp -- all persist into the second half. Full H1 results in late August 2026 and Q3 results around October 2026 could each print another loss and a further cash-balance drawdown as the payables float reverses with softer volumes. There is no debt maturity wall (only RMB 4.4B total debt), so the danger is earnings and cash erosion, not insolvency -- but a second loss-making quarter would break the 'temporary cost shock' framing and could retest the HK$40 low.
positioning_washout: The Hong Kong line is structurally fragile: only about 100.2M H-shares (~6% of the ~1.74B total) were floated on 5 November 2025 at HK$131.50, and the price has since collapsed to the low-HK$40s -- a thin, momentum-driven float that has already absorbed heavy forced selling from disappointed IPO buyers. The larger A-share (601127) hit limit-down on 13 July 2026, its lowest since March 2024. There is no dividend-cut mechanic forcing a yield-holder exodus, but the small float means liquidity-driven air-pockets in both directions; a further profit disappointment could trigger another mechanical leg down before value buyers step in near net cash.
moderator_conclusion: Seres is a genuine cash-backed franchise caught in China's electric-vehicle margin war, and the timing is awkward: the deep-value screen flagged it near its lows in the very half-year it swung from a RMB 2.94B profit to a RMB 1.5-1.8B loss. The bull plank -- roughly HK$37-38 of net cash plus a Huawei-ecosystem stake under a HK$47.8 quote -- is real but softened by the fact that much of that cash is supplier float on ~187-day payables, not distributable shareholder capital, and by a moat that is visibly eroding as Huawei lends the same technology to AITO's rivals. Reconciled sum-of-the-parts fair value is about HK$48, essentially the current price: the cash cushion and the now-negative operating earnings roughly offset. That leaves a balanced-to-poor risk/reward at HK$47.8 -- meaningful downside toward HK$34 if losses persist and the float reverses, upside toward HK$65 only if the second-half recovery lands -- and no hard catalyst to force the issue. This is a wait, not a buy: the setup becomes attractive nearer net cash (about HK$37-40, the year's low) or once Q3 2026 results confirm margins are actually recovering. Until one of those arrives, the discount is thin and the trajectory is pointed the wrong way. Separately, judged purely on value with no catalyst overlay, the case is held back by the same two facts -- the trailing cheapness is a peak-earnings artifact now that profit has gone negative, and the moat is eroding -- which cap the value conviction low regardless of the cash.

# Forensic Dossier — Seres Group Co., Ltd. (9927.HK / A-share 601127.SS)

*Prepared for the investment committee. No earnings-call transcript was available for this
listing — the paid data feed carries neither transcripts nor news for the Hong Kong line, so
this dossier is built from the reported financials (in Chinese yuan, RMB) and dated public
disclosures gathered from company results releases, regulatory filings and trade press. Where
management "voice" would normally be quoted, I substitute the hard record and the company's own
dated profit warning.*

Seres is the Chinese premium electric-vehicle maker behind the AITO (Wenjie) brand, built jointly
with Huawei since 2021. It carries two listings: the main A-share in Shanghai (601127) and a
Hong Kong H-share (9927), floated on 5 November 2025 at HK$131.50. This note values the H-share.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story has moved through three distinct chapters in barely two years. **Chapter one (2021-2023):
a money-losing contract assembler.** Revenue sat at RMB 16.7B (2021), RMB 34.1B (2022) and RMB 35.8B
(2023) while the company lost money every year (net losses of RMB 1.8B, 3.8B and 2.5B). **Chapter two
(2024: the Huawei breakout).** The AITO M9 flagship sport-utility vehicle launched into the RMB 400,000-plus
luxury segment and revenue exploded to RMB 145.2B, with the first full-year profit of RMB 5.95B. This is
the number that anchors every bull. **Chapter three (2025-2026: the plateau and the crack).** Revenue grew
only +13.7% to RMB 165.1B in 2025 and profit essentially flatlined at RMB 5.96B — and then, in the first
half of 2026, the story broke. On 12-13 July 2026 the company pre-announced a first-half **loss** of
RMB 1.5-1.8B, versus a RMB 2.94B profit a year earlier. The growth narrative has quietly been replaced by
a cost-and-competition narrative.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management framing | The financial record | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Record year — RMB 165B revenue, RMB 5.96B profit" (2025 results, Apr 2026) | True as stated, but revenue growth decelerated from roughly +300% (2024) to +13.7% (2025) and profit was flat year-on-year | Accurate but flattering — the momentum was already gone |
| "China's answer to Mercedes-Benz and BMW" (Apr 2026 results release) | Premium positioning is real (AITO M9 at RMB 479,800), but net margin was only 3.6% in 2025 and turned negative in H1 2026 | Aspirational; the economics are not yet premium |
| "AITO sales buck the trend, +10% growth" (July 2026 warning) | Total new-energy-vehicle volume rose only +3.87% to 178,777 units in H1 2026; AITO deliveries +10.2% | True but thin — a fraction of the 2024 growth rate |
| Implied earnings power ~RMB 6B/year | Q3 2025 profit RMB 2.37B → Q4 2025 RMB 0.64B → Q1 2026 RMB 0.75B → Q2 2026 an AITO standalone loss of RMB 2.25-2.55B | The earnings base is collapsing sequentially, not compounding |

The single most important divergence: the market and the screener still carry a ~RMB 6B annual-profit
anchor, but the **quarter-by-quarter path shows profit falling off a cliff** — from RMB 2.37B in the third
quarter of 2025 to an outright loss by the second quarter of 2026. The "deep value" screen (price near the
52-week low, low multiple on trailing earnings) is measuring a peak that has already passed.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining.** With no transcript, the cleanest read on management confidence is their own disclosure cadence.
As recently as the April 2026 annual release the framing was offensive and expansive ("record high", "path to
become China's Mercedes/BMW"). By 12 July 2026 the language turned defensive and apologetic: the loss was
blamed on "sustained price increases for key upstream raw materials such as memory chips, industrial metals
and lithium carbonate", an inability to pass those costs on "due to intense competition", and "asset impairment
losses" on equipment and inventory made obsolete by "accelerating technological iteration". The company itself
listed three forward uncertainties — raw-material volatility, an escalating price war, and slower-than-expected
ramp of new models. That is a management on the back foot.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Medium, trending lower.** Seres does not issue formal quarterly guidance, so this is judged on delivered
results versus the prevailing narrative. The 2024 breakout was over-delivered against a low base — genuinely
impressive. But the 2025-2026 arc shows the opposite: the "record profit" framing of April 2026 was followed
within three months by a profit warning that swung the half-year from a RMB 2.94B profit to a loss. Nothing in
the disclosures ahead of that warning prepared investors for a per-vehicle loss exceeding RMB 20,000 at AITO in
the second quarter. A management team whose "premium franchise" message is contradicted by a swing to losses one
quarter later has, at minimum, a timing-and-candor problem. Reliability: **Medium.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

The recurring, unresolved questions around this name are structural, not cosmetic:
- **Single-partner dependence.** AITO is built on Huawei's smart-car stack. Huawei has since extended the same
  Harmony Intelligent Mobility Alliance (HIMA) technology to rivals — Luxeed (with Chery), Stelato (with BAIC),
  Maextro (with JAC) — diluting AITO's exclusivity. Management has not credibly answered how AITO defends its
  position as Huawei spreads the same capability across competitors.
- **Margin durability.** The July warning confirmed the bears: when input costs rise, Seres cannot raise price
  in China's price war, so the margin is the shock absorber. There is no answer yet to how the company earns a
  sustainable premium margin.
- **What the cash is.** The balance sheet shows RMB 59.5B net cash, but also RMB 66B of payables on ~187-day
  terms. Much of the "cash" is supplier float that reverses if volumes fall — a point the profit warning makes
  urgent.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 First-half 2026 swing from a RMB 2.94B profit to a RMB 1.5-1.8B loss (announced 12-13 July 2026).
🔴 AITO — the core brand — is the main loss driver, with a Q2 2026 standalone loss of RMB 2.25-2.55B.
🔴 Asset impairments on tooling and inventory: models are being obsoleted faster than they are being depreciated.
🔴 Margin has no defense in the price war; cost inflation flows straight to the bottom line.
🔴 Huawei is diluting AITO's exclusivity by partnering with rival automakers on the same technology.
🔴 The H-share collapsed from its HK$131.50 float price (Nov 2025) to the low-HK$40s — a tiny ~6% public float dumped hard.
🟢 Net cash of RMB 59.5B against a Hong Kong market value of roughly RMB 76B — a genuine, if partly float-funded, cushion.
🟢 Volume is still growing (+10% at AITO in H1 2026) into a soft market, and the new-generation M9 drew 10,000+ orders within three weeks of its 27 May 2026 launch.
🟢 A ~10% stake in Huawei's smart-car unit (Yinwang), carried at ~RMB 13.4B, aligns Seres to the ecosystem it depends on.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The most telling shift is in what the company now discusses. In 2024-2025 the vocabulary was volume, premium
positioning and record revenue. By mid-2026 the same management is talking about "raw material costs",
"impairment", "technological iteration cycles" and "price war" — the language of a manufacturer defending a
margin, not a brand extending a lead. The impairment charge is the quiet tell: writing down equipment and
inventory because model cycles are "accelerating" is an admission that the capital intensity of staying premium
in this segment is rising faster than the pricing power to fund it. Separately, the large first-quarter 2026 cash
outflow (net cash fell from RMB 82.7B to RMB 59.5B) reflects a sizable distribution and a ~RMB 13B move into the
Yinwang investment — capital allocation is active, not passive, which cuts both ways.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: DETERIORATING.** This is a 2024 breakout that has run into China's electric-vehicle margin war.
Volume still grows, but profitability has inverted — the very quarter the deep-value screen flagged the name near
its lows is the quarter the company swung to a loss.

**Moat: ERODING.** The advantage was always the Huawei relationship — the software, the brand halo, the retail
reach. That advantage is intact but no longer exclusive: Huawei now lends the same stack to Chery, BAIC and JAC.
Meanwhile the returns evidence points the wrong way — a 3.6% net margin in 2025 that has turned negative, with
return on invested capital that the screener reads as negative. A high-but-falling (now negative) margin is an
eroding moat, not a wide one. **Moat trend: ERODING.**

**Secular threat: MATERIAL, not terminal.** The structural force here is commoditization and margin deflation
across Chinese new-energy vehicles — real and unresolved, but AITO is a premium brand with growing volume and a
powerful technology partner, so this is a competitive margin squeeze rather than a melting terminal value. The
cheapness is therefore neither a clean fear-print nor a pure value trap: it is a genuine cash-backed franchise
whose earning power is, for now, unproven at the price.

**The single thing the director must weigh before sizing:** the reported RMB 59.5B net cash is the whole bull
case, and a large part of it is supplier float (RMB 66B of payables on ~187-day terms) that would drain if
volumes and the payables cycle reverse. Size the position to the cash you would actually keep in a downturn, not
the headline number.

Against a Hong Kong market value of about RMB 76B (1.74B shares at HK$47.8, converted at roughly 1.10 Hong Kong dollars per yuan), net cash alone is worth about HK$37-38 per share -- close to four-fifths of the quote. On top of the cash sits a roughly 10% stake in Huawei's smart-car unit (Yinwang), carried near RMB 13.4B. Strip both out and the market is paying only a low-single-digit multiple for a business that did RMB 165B of revenue and RMB 5.96B of profit in 2025. consensus_delta: For a deep-value name the question is whether the street is pricing terminal decline into stable earnings power -- here it is closer to the reverse. forcing_function: There is no hard, dated, binding forcing function. The realistic re-rating triggers are soft: (1) H1 2026 results in late August 2026 and Q3 results around October 2026 -- the first evidence of whether the second-half margin recovery is real; (2) monthly AITO delivery prints showing the new M9/M8 cycle restoring scale; (3) any capital-return announcement that converts the cash pile into shareholder value. the headline number.

bull_thesis: Seres builds the AITO range of premium electric and range-extended sport-utility vehicles in Chongqing, and the bull case rests on a simple observation: what broke in 2026 was the price of the cars, not the demand for them. In the first half of 2026 the company sold 196,580 vehicles, down just 1.02% from a year earlier, and electric units actually rose 3.87% to 178,777. Revenue fell 7.87% to CNY 57.49 billion and gross margin fell 4.7 percentage points to 21.8%, which means almost all of the damage came from price and input cost rather than from customers walking away. Management named the culprits precisely in the 19 August 2026 half-year report: the average daily price of battery-grade lithium carbonate rose 132.2% year on year, and automotive-grade chips ran into what the company called structural shortages and sharp price increases. Those are cyclical commodity inputs, not a broken franchise. Strip out the CNY 1.75 billion non-cash write-down of intangible assets and the CNY 1.72 billion reported loss becomes a few percentage points of operating slippage on a CNY 57.5 billion revenue base. The second leg of the case is the 15 September 2026 restructuring of the Huawei relationship. Huawei handed Seres operational control of AITO, transferring product definition, vehicle design, brand marketing, retail channels and service operations, while AITO stays inside Huawei's HIMA alliance and keeps buying Huawei's driving software. Seres already bought the AITO trademarks and design patents outright for CNY 2.5 billion in July 2024. The optimistic reading is that a company that was paid only to manufacture now owns the customer relationship and the retail margin that went with it, for the first time. The third leg is the balance sheet. The company holds CNY 73.13 billion of cash and short-term investments against roughly CNY 4.35 billion of genuine interest-bearing borrowing, and it owns 10% of Shenzhen Yinwang, Huawei's intelligent-automotive unit, bought for CNY 11.5 billion in August 2024 and carried at about CNY 13.5 billion. Yinwang supplies driving software to every brand in the alliance and to outside customers, and that stake earns no line in Seres's profit that an investor would notice. Finally, the starting point is unusually low. The Hong Kong line at HK$35.14 values the entire company, all 1.742 billion shares, at about CNY 52 billion against roughly CNY 160 billion of revenue. Analyst consensus has 2026 as the trough at CNY 0.44 of earnings per share and 2027 at CNY 3.05, which would put the Hong Kong line under 10 times forward earnings before any credit for cash. For this case to work, three things must hold: lithium and chip costs must stop rising, the independent AITO sales network must be built without a second year of margin destruction, and the second half of 2026 must deliver the sharp seasonal recovery both 2024 and 2025 produced.
bear_thesis: The bear case is that the one thing that made Seres valuable has just been handed back to it, and the cheapness that makes the shares look compelling is an accounting illusion. Start with the partnership. Huawei did not merely manufacture a change of administration on 15 September 2026; it withdrew from the brand it built first while retaining operational leadership of the four other alliance marques, Luxeed, Stelato, Maextro and Shangjie. The ordering is the message. Huawei's product definition, brand marketing and retail network were the moat, rented rather than owned, and Seres must now reproduce a national retail machine from a standing start, while volumes fall and a price war runs. That build is a fixed-cost commitment landing on a business whose selling and administrative expense already ran CNY 5.37 billion in the second quarter alone, seventeen percent of revenue. The competitive evidence is already visible. Huawei's HIMA alliance delivered about 192,000 units from January to May 2026, up 26.5% year on year, while Seres's own revenue fell about 8% across the half. Seres cut the entry price of the M6 by CNY 50,000, from CNY 279,800 to CNY 229,800, in June 2026, an 18% cut on the trim that anchors the range. Management describes its decision not to raise prices as a choice to maintain premium supply standards; the filed numbers describe a company with no pricing power cutting into a cost shock. Both figures are true and both are misleading. That cash is financed by CNY 38.8 billion of notes payable to suppliers and CNY 19.9 billion of trade payables. Net working capital is CNY 3.84 billion. A cash pile that moves twenty billion on working-capital timing is not a floor under the share price; it is a liability that happens to sit on the asset side. Quality is thin elsewhere too. positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure has been severe and is probably not finished. The Hong Kong listing came on 5 November 2025 at HK$131.5, valuing the company near CNY 196 billion against CNY 165 billion of revenue, roughly 1.2 times revenue for a vehicle assembler at a moment when the closest comparables traded near 0.55 to 0.65 times. moderator_conclusion: Wait for the wash-out. This is a genuinely cheap asset with a genuinely weakened competitive position, and the two facts do not cancel out. The case for patience rather than a pass is that the damage in the first half of 2026 was to price and cost, not to demand: the company sold 196,580 vehicles, down barely 1%, and electric units grew, while gross margin fell 4.7 points to 21.8% on a 132.2% rise in lithium carbonate prices and a chip shortage. We judge the fair value of the Hong Kong line at HK$46.50, about 32% above the HK$35.14 price, against an adverse case of HK$23.50 about 33% below it. That is a coin flip dressed as a bargain, and the resolution point is five weeks away in the third-quarter report. interrogator_dossier:
# Forensic Dossier — Seres Group Co., Ltd (9927.HK / 601127.SS)

**Date of review:** 2026-09-22 · **Price used:** HK$35.14 (Hong Kong listing, HKD) · **Shanghai A-line:** CNY 47.78

**A note on sources before anything else.** No earnings-call transcript exists for this company in our licensed data feed, and Chinese A-share issuers with a Hong Kong secondary listing do not hold the quarterly analyst calls that American companies do. There is therefore no multi-quarter transcript arc to read. Everything below is built from the company's own filed numbers (eight quarters of income statement, balance sheet and cash flow), its 12 July 2026 profit warning, its 19 August 2026 half-year report, and dated trade-press coverage of the Huawei partnership. Where I quote, I quote the filed half-year report as relayed by CnEVPost on 19 August 2026. I have invented nothing, and where a fact could not be verified I say so.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Seres makes the AITO (Wenjie) range of premium electric and range-extended sport-utility vehicles in Chongqing. It is not really an ordinary carmaker. Until one week ago it was the manufacturing half of a partnership in which Huawei did almost everything that touches the customer — defined the product, designed the vehicle, built the brand, and sold the cars through its own retail network — while Seres built them. That arrangement is what turned a loss-making minivan maker into a company with CNY 165 billion of revenue.

The arc across the last three years is one of the steepest in the industry, in both directions.

**2021 to 2023 — the pre-Huawei company.** Revenue of CNY 16.7 billion in 2021 rising to CNY 35.8 billion in 2023, with losses every year: CNY 1.82 billion, CNY 3.83 billion, CNY 2.45 billion. This was a subscale manufacturer going nowhere.

**2024 to 2025 — the Huawei years.** Revenue quadrupled to CNY 145.2 billion in 2024 and CNY 165.1 billion in 2025, and the company made money for the first time: CNY 5.95 billion and CNY 5.96 billion of net income. Gross margin reached 29.1% in 2025 — extraordinary for a volume carmaker and a direct product of Huawei's brand pricing power. Management spent heavily to secure the relationship: CNY 2.5 billion in July 2024 for the AITO trademarks and design patents, and CNY 11.5 billion in August 2024 for a 10% stake in Shenzhen Yinwang, Huawei's intelligent-automotive unit (the deal completed in September 2025). On 5 November 2025 the company listed in Hong Kong at HK$131.5 a share, raising roughly CNY 12.9 billion.

**2026 — the unwind.** The story since has contracted on every axis. First-half revenue fell 7.87% to CNY 57.49 billion, gross margin fell 4.7 percentage points to 21.8%, and the company swung to a net loss of CNY 1.72 billion from a CNY 2.94 billion profit a year earlier. In June the company cut the entry price of the new M6 by CNY 50,000, from CNY 279,800 to CNY 229,800 — an 18% cut on the trim that sets the brand's price floor. Then on 15 September 2026 Huawei handed operational control of AITO back to Seres: product definition, vehicle design, brand marketing, retail channels and service operations all transfer. AITO stays inside Huawei's HIMA alliance and keeps buying Huawei's driving software, but Seres must now build and fund its own sales network.

**What was quietly added.** While the core brand was shrinking, 2026 saw a remarkable burst of new initiatives: a premium-charging joint venture with BMW and Mercedes (17 April), a new vehicle brand connected to ByteDance (3 June), a second new brand called Aiva through affiliate Saidou (9 June), a humanoid robot (15 June), and a United Arab Emirates dealership (6 February). Five new directions in five months, from a company whose one profitable product line was losing share.

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

The company's explanation for the half-year loss is specific and testable. It blames input costs — battery-grade lithium carbonate up 132.2% year on year on an average daily price basis, plus "structural shortages and sharp price increases" in automotive-grade chips — and says it chose not to pass those costs to customers. It also took a CNY 1.75 billion write-down of intangible assets, attributed to "rapid technological iteration in the NEV industry."

| Management's claim | What the filed numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| The problem is input costs, not demand | Unit sales were 196,580, down only 1.02%; electric-vehicle units actually rose 3.87% to 178,777. Revenue fell 7.87%, so the average selling price fell about 7%. Gross margin fell 4.7 points. | **Largely supported.** Volume held; price and cost did the damage. This is genuinely a margin event, not a demand collapse. |
| "We declined to pass these costs to customers" | True in the sense that prices were not raised — but the company went the other way and *cut* the M6 entry price by CNY 50,000 in June. | **Poorer than the story.** This is not restraint; it is the absence of pricing power, described kindly. |
| Scale is still building | Half-year revenue of CNY 57.49 billion is below the CNY 62.40 billion of a year earlier; the second half of 2025 alone did CNY 102.6 billion. The business is running below its own recent peak. | **Diverges.** |
| The write-down reflects industry pace | The CNY 1.75 billion charge sits against CNY 12.3 billion of intangible assets carried on the balance sheet, much of it capitalised development spending. Writing off capitalised development because technology moved on is the textbook sign that the spending was capitalised too aggressively in the first place. | **Concerning.** The charge is honest; what it reveals about the earlier accounting is not flattering. |
| The balance sheet is a fortress — cash above CNY 73.15 billion, 57% of total assets, with interest-bearing debt only 3.2% of assets | Both figures are accurate. But the cash is funded by supplier credit: CNY 38.8 billion of notes payable to suppliers plus CNY 19.9 billion of trade payables. Net working capital is only CNY 3.84 billion. The company collects from customers in about 8 days and pays suppliers in about 61. | **Accurate but seriously misleading if read as spare cash.** See section 6. |

**The single most important forensic finding in this file** concerns that cash. In the first quarter of 2026, operating cash flow was *minus CNY 20.95 billion* in three months — the supplier float draining after the year-end volume push. The second quarter put CNY 8.47 billion back. Across the half, operating cash flow was minus CNY 12.38 billion. A cash balance that swings by twenty billion on working-capital timing is not a store of value the way an investor instinctively reads "57% of assets are cash." It is the float of a business that is paid instantly and pays late, and it shrinks when volumes shrink.

**Two numbers in our own screener file are wrong and must not be used.** The scan reports price-to-free-cash-flow of 2.0x and a discounted-cash-flow fair value of 198.1 — both computed from the 2025 peak-year cash flow. On a trailing twelve-month basis free cash flow is *minus* CNY 3.27 billion. The screener's net-debt field is also wrong; the corrected balance-sheet figure is in section 6.

---

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rating: Declining**, judged from disclosure behaviour rather than call transcripts, since none exist.

The sequence is telling. On **12 July 2026** the company issued a profit warning flagging a half-year net loss of CNY 1.5 billion to CNY 1.8 billion and naming the causes as rising material costs and asset write-downs. On **19 August 2026** it reported a loss of CNY 1.72 billion — inside its own range, and close to the middle of it. That is competent, unpanicked disclosure and it deserves credit.

But the *content* of the disclosure has shifted from offensive to defensive in one year. The 2025 language was about scale, premium positioning and a 29% gross margin. The 2026 language is about lithium prices, chip shortages, write-downs and "maintaining premium supply standards" — the vocabulary of a management team explaining a result rather than setting a direction. Research and development spending rose 27.4% to CNY 3.73 billion into a shrinking revenue base, which reads as commitment rather than retreat; but it sits alongside five new ventures launched in five months, which reads as a company casting about for the next story because the current one has stopped working.

---

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Score: Medium.**

The evidence that exists is good. The July warning was issued roughly five weeks before the result, gave a numerical range, named the causes, and the reported figure landed inside it. Chinese issuers are required to warn on large swings, so this is compliance rather than virtue — but plenty of companies warn late, warn vaguely, or warn low and then miss their own range. Seres did none of those.

Against that, the screener's earnings-beat record is 2 of the last 4 quarters, a 50% hit rate, which is coin-flip. And there is a structural pattern the director should hold in mind: this company's results are extremely back-half-weighted. The first half of 2025 was CNY 62.4 billion of revenue against CNY 102.6 billion in the second half. The same shape is embedded in the current consensus, which expects CNY 159.3 billion for full-year 2026 against CNY 57.5 billion delivered in the first half — implying a second half of roughly CNY 102 billion, essentially matching the prior year's record second half at a moment when the brand is losing share. That is a demanding number and it has not been de-risked.

---

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

With no calls, the pressure points must be inferred from what the company does and does not quantify. Three stand out.

**The Huawei dependency was never quantified, and now it is changing.** Seres has never disclosed what it pays Huawei — for the driving software, for the retail channel, for the brand. The 15 September restructuring changes all of those economics at once, and the company disclosed no new fee or equity arrangement alongside it. An investor is being asked to underwrite a transition whose cost is undisclosed.

**AITO's own volumes are not broken out.** The company reports total units. The alliance-level data that is public tells an uncomfortable story: Huawei's HIMA alliance delivered about 192,000 units from January to May 2026, up 26.5% year on year, while Seres's revenue fell 8% over the half. The alliance is growing; Seres's share of it is not. In August, HIMA deliveries themselves turned negative, down 5.52% year on year.

**Nobody has been made to explain the working-capital swing.** A negative CNY 20.95 billion operating quarter in a company that headlines its cash position is the question I would ask first, and there is no public forum in which it has been asked.

There is a further gap worth stating plainly: I could find no dated analyst price target for the Hong Kong line. Our data provider has no price-target coverage for this listing, and the web-search budget for this session was exhausted before a broker target could be sourced. I therefore use no target figure anywhere in this file.

---

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 **The cash is supplier float, not a war chest.** Cash and short-term investments of CNY 73.13 billion are financed by CNY 38.8 billion of supplier notes and CNY 19.9 billion of trade payables. Netting the supplier notes and the CNY 4.35 billion of genuine borrowings leaves roughly **CNY 30 billion of defensible net cash** — about CNY 17.2 a share, or HK$20.1. The company's own framing (debt is 3.2% of assets) implies nearly CNY 69 billion, which would be more than the entire Hong Kong-line market value. I do not accept that framing, and the first quarter's cash flow is the reason.

🔴 **Returns on capital have gone to nothing.** Trailing return on equity is 3.6% and return on invested capital 0.7%. The screener's full-year figures are worse still. A company earning less on its capital than it can earn on a bank deposit is not compounding.

🔴 **Capitalised development spending written off.** CNY 1.75 billion of intangibles impaired for "rapid technological iteration," against CNY 12.3 billion still carried. A further CNY 2.31 billion sits in "other gains and losses."

🔴 **The partner stepped back from this brand and only this brand.** Huawei retains operational leadership of the other four HIMA marques — Luxeed, Stelato, Maextro and Shangjie. It handed back the one it had built first. That ordering matters.

🔴 **Five new ventures in five months** while the core brand shrank: a charging joint venture, a ByteDance-linked brand, the Aiva brand, a humanoid robot, a Gulf dealership. Each is a call on management attention and capital.

🔴 **The listing itself was sold at a peak.** The November 2025 initial public offering priced at HK$131.5, valuing the whole company near CNY 196 billion on CNY 165 billion of revenue — roughly 1.2x revenue for a vehicle assembler, when the closest listed comparables trade around 0.55x to 0.65x. Much of the 73% decline since is the deflation of that price, not new information.

🟢 **Volume held.** Units fell only 1.02% and electric units rose 3.87%. The franchise did not lose its customers; it lost its price.

🟢 **The loss is smaller than it looks.** Strip the CNY 1.75 billion write-down and the half-year result is an operating stumble of a few percent on CNY 57.5 billion of revenue, not a structural cash loss.

🟢 **Seres now owns the customer.** Whatever the execution risk, product definition, design, brand and retail all move in-house from 15 September. The retail margin Huawei captured is now Seres's to capture — and Seres already owns the AITO trademarks outright.

🟢 **A real, under-recognised financial asset.** The 10% stake in Huawei's Yinwang unit, bought for CNY 11.5 billion and carried at about CNY 13.5 billion, is a minority interest in the supplier of driving software to the entire HIMA alliance and to third parties. It earns no line in the income statement that an investor would notice.

🟢 **Honest pre-announcement.** The July warning was specific, early and accurate.

---

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

**The language of the 15 September announcement is the signal.** Huawei transferred "product definition, product design, brand marketing, retail channels and service operations." That is not a delegation of tasks; it is the return of an entire commercial function. Read one way it is a promotion — Seres graduates from contract manufacturer to brand owner. Read the other way, the party that made the brand work has decided its time is better spent on four other brands, and the manufacturer now has to reproduce Huawei's retail machine from a standing start, with falling volumes, in a price war. Both readings are available from the same sentence. The second is the one the share price is pricing.

**The sequencing of the write-down.** The impairment of capitalised development landed in the same half as the loss of product-definition authority. Intangible assets are written down when the cash flows behind them shrink. It is hard not to read the charge as an early, quiet acknowledgement of the September change.

**A tell in the working capital.** Days of payables outstanding is about 61 against 8 days of receivables and 7 days of inventory — a cash conversion cycle of minus 47 days. That is a supplier-financed model. It works beautifully at scale and reverses violently on the way down, which is exactly what the first quarter showed.

**A new voice, and what it is selling.** The 2026 initiative list — robotics, an internet-company car brand, a charging network with German luxury marques — is the vocabulary of a company that wants to be valued as a technology platform rather than an assembler. That ambition is not yet visible anywhere in the returns on capital.

---

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: DETERIORATING**, with a genuine restructuring underway that could change the label but has not yet.

Revenue is down 8%, gross margin down 4.7 points, the company has swung to a loss, operating cash flow ran minus CNY 12.38 billion in the half, and the brand is losing share inside an alliance that is growing. The Huawei handover is a real pivot and may prove to be the right one, but it is one week old and entirely unproven.

**The single thing the director must weigh before sizing this:** almost all of the apparent cheapness is a balance-sheet add-back, not an earnings discount. Value the whole company on revenue with no cash credit and the Hong Kong line trades at roughly 0.33x revenue against 0.65x for Li Auto and 0.55x for Leapmotor — a discount, but a defensible one for a brand losing relative share. Credit the CNY 30 billion of net cash and the operating business is being valued at almost nothing. The entire investment case turns on whether that cash is spare or is supplier float that a volume decline would consume. On the first quarter's evidence, it is a great deal more float than spare. Size the position to the version of the balance sheet you actually believe, not the version the company presents.

**Economic moat.** The moat here was never Seres's. It was Huawei's brand, Huawei's driving software and Huawei's retail network, rented to a manufacturer that supplied the factory. The type is best described as intangible-brand and channel access, held on loan. The evidence says it is narrowing on every measure the returns provide: gross margin from 29.1% in 2025 to 21.8% in the first half of 2026, return on invested capital down to 0.7%, pricing cut by CNY 50,000 on the entry trim, and the brand shrinking while its own alliance grew 26.5% through May. By the returns-and-margin test this is an eroding moat, not a wide one, and the 15 September transfer of channel and brand authority is the formal confirmation of that erosion rather than a cure for it.

**Terminal value.** The threat is real but not terminal. China's electric-vehicle market is growing, not shrinking, so this is not a melting base. The structural risk is different: in a vehicle built around someone else's driving software and sold through someone else's shops, the durable economics accrue to the software and channel owner, and the assembler is commoditised. Seres has partially hedged that — it owns 10% of Yinwang and it owns the AITO marks — but it has not escaped it. I judge the secular threat **material, not terminal**, and note that none of the eight named structural forces in our own controlled vocabulary describes this risk; forcing one on would be false precision.

**Fear-print or value trap?** Neither cleanly. It is a genuine de-rating from a genuinely absurd listing price, on top of a real margin shock, in a business whose competitive position got weaker in the same quarter. The cheapness is real on a revenue basis and overstated on a cash basis. That combination argues for patience and a small size, not for conviction in either direction.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a moat that is being eroded · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.

bull_thesis: Seres builds the AITO range of premium electric and range-extended sport-utility vehicles in Chongqing, and the bull case rests on a simple observation: what broke in 2026 was the price of the cars, not the demand for them. In the first half of 2026 the company sold 196,580 vehicles, down just 1.02% from a year earlier, and electric units actually rose 3.87% to 178,777. Revenue fell 7.87% to CNY 57.49 billion and gross margin fell 4.7 percentage points to 21.8%, which means almost all of the damage came from price and input cost rather than from customers walking away. Management named the culprits precisely in the 19 August 2026 half-year report: the average daily price of battery-grade lithium carbonate rose 132.2% year on year, and automotive-grade chips ran into what the company called structural shortages and sharp price increases. Those are cyclical commodity inputs, not a broken franchise. Strip out the CNY 1.75 billion non-cash write-down of intangible assets and the CNY 1.72 billion reported loss becomes a few percentage points of operating slippage on a CNY 57.5 billion revenue base. The second leg of the case is the 15 September 2026 restructuring of the Huawei relationship. Huawei handed Seres operational control of AITO, transferring product definition, vehicle design, brand marketing, retail channels and service operations, while AITO stays inside Huawei's HIMA alliance and keeps buying Huawei's driving software. Seres already bought the AITO trademarks and design patents outright for CNY 2.5 billion in July 2024. The optimistic reading is that a company that was paid only to manufacture now owns the customer relationship and the retail margin that went with it, for the first time. The third leg is the balance sheet. The company holds CNY 73.13 billion of cash and short-term investments against roughly CNY 4.35 billion of genuine interest-bearing borrowing, and it owns 10% of Shenzhen Yinwang, Huawei's intelligent-automotive unit, bought for CNY 11.5 billion in August 2024 and carried at about CNY 13.5 billion. Yinwang supplies driving software to every brand in the alliance and to outside customers, and that stake earns no line in Seres's profit that an investor would notice. Finally, the starting point is unusually low. The Hong Kong line at HK$35.14 values the entire company, all 1.742 billion shares, at about CNY 52 billion against roughly CNY 160 billion of revenue. Analyst consensus has 2026 as the trough at CNY 0.44 of earnings per share and 2027 at CNY 3.05, which would put the Hong Kong line under 10 times forward earnings before any credit for cash. For this case to work, three things must hold: lithium and chip costs must stop rising, the independent AITO sales network must be built without a second year of margin destruction, and the second half of 2026 must deliver the sharp seasonal recovery both 2024 and 2025 produced.
bear_thesis: The bear case is that the one thing that made Seres valuable has just been handed back to it, and the cheapness that makes the shares look compelling is an accounting illusion. Start with the partnership. Huawei did not merely manufacture a change of administration on 15 September 2026; it withdrew from the brand it built first while retaining operational leadership of the four other alliance marques, Luxeed, Stelato, Maextro and Shangjie. The ordering is the message. Huawei's product definition, brand marketing and retail network were the moat, rented rather than owned, and Seres must now reproduce a national retail machine from a standing start, while volumes fall and a price war runs. That build is a fixed-cost commitment landing on a business whose selling and administrative expense already ran CNY 5.37 billion in the second quarter alone, seventeen percent of revenue. The competitive evidence is already visible. Huawei's HIMA alliance delivered about 192,000 units from January to May 2026, up 26.5% year on year, while Seres's own revenue fell about 8% across the half. The alliance grew; AITO's share of it shrank. By August, alliance deliveries themselves turned negative, down 5.52% year on year. Seres cut the entry price of the M6 by CNY 50,000, from CNY 279,800 to CNY 229,800, in June 2026, an 18% cut on the trim that anchors the range. Management describes its decision not to raise prices as a choice to maintain premium supply standards; the filed numbers describe a company with no pricing power cutting into a cost shock. Then the balance sheet, which is where the real risk sits. The company presents cash above CNY 73.15 billion as 57% of total assets with interest-bearing debt at only 3.2% of assets. Both figures are true and both are misleading. That cash is financed by CNY 38.8 billion of notes payable to suppliers and CNY 19.9 billion of trade payables. Net working capital is CNY 3.84 billion. The company collects from customers in roughly 8 days and pays suppliers in roughly 61, a cash conversion cycle of minus 47 days, and in the first quarter of 2026 that float ran backwards: operating cash flow was minus CNY 20.95 billion in three months, and minus CNY 12.38 billion across the half. Trailing free cash flow is minus CNY 3.27 billion. A cash pile that moves twenty billion on working-capital timing is not a floor under the share price; it is a liability that happens to sit on the asset side. Quality is thin elsewhere too. Trailing return on invested capital is 0.7% and return on equity 3.6%. The company wrote off CNY 1.75 billion of capitalised development spending for rapid technological iteration, against CNY 12.3 billion still carried, with a further CNY 2.31 billion of other losses. And while the core brand shrank, management launched five new ventures in five months: a charging joint venture with BMW and Mercedes in April, a ByteDance-linked vehicle brand in June, the Aiva brand in June, a humanoid robot in June, and a Gulf dealership in February. That is attention and capital leaving the one business that works. Finally, the consensus that makes the shares look cheap is itself demanding: full-year 2026 revenue of CNY 159.3 billion against CNY 57.5 billion delivered in the first half implies a second half of roughly CNY 102 billion, matching the record second half of 2025 at the exact moment the brand is losing relative share. Confirmation of the bear case would be a third-quarter print in late October showing gross margin still near 21%, a second consecutive quarter of negative operating cash flow, or disclosed spending on the new sales network that exceeds the retail margin it is meant to capture.
consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market is narrower than the 73% share-price decline would suggest, and it runs in both directions. The market appears to be treating this as a demand collapse. It is not: first-half 2026 unit sales fell only 1.02% and electric units rose 3.87%, so the franchise kept its customers and lost its price. On that point we are more positive than the tape. But we are markedly more negative than the company's own presentation of its balance sheet. Management frames cash above CNY 73.15 billion, 57% of total assets, against interest-bearing debt of only 3.2% of assets, which implies nearly CNY 69 billion of net cash, more than the entire Hong Kong-line market value. We treat the CNY 38.8 billion of notes payable to suppliers as debt, which cuts defensible net cash to about CNY 30 billion, and then haircut that again for the float a shrinking business consumes. The first quarter of 2026 settles the argument: operating cash flow of minus CNY 20.95 billion in three months is not what a fortress balance sheet does. Our second disagreement is with the sell side on 2027. Consensus of CNY 3.05 of earnings per share requires both a margin recovery and a volume recovery in a brand whose partner has just stepped back and which must fund a new retail network; we underwrite the revenue but not the multiple that number would normally earn.
forcing_function: There is no single event that forces a re-rating here, which is the central weakness of the setup. The closest thing is the third-quarter report due in late October 2026: a gross margin printing back above 24%, positive operating cash flow, and a credible disclosed budget for the new retail network would be the three-part proof that the margin shock was cyclical and the Huawei handover is a promotion rather than a demotion. Any two of those would justify revisiting this at a larger size. Beyond that, the real forcing function is commodity, not corporate: lithium carbonate prices rolling over would restore several points of gross margin across the whole sector, Seres included. That is exactly the kind of single shared macro driver we are wary of underwriting, and we take no credit for it.
valley_of_death: The risky window is the next two to three quarters, and it has a specific shape. Third-quarter results land in late October 2026, roughly five weeks out, and they will be the first print to show whether the second-half seasonal recovery that carried 2024 and 2025 is still intact. Consensus needs a second half of roughly CNY 102 billion of revenue against CNY 57.5 billion delivered in the first half, which would match the record second half of 2025 at the moment the brand is losing relative share. If that does not arrive, the full-year 2026 consensus of CNY 0.44 of earnings per share is the first casualty and the 2027 recovery number is the second. Layered on top, the independent sales network must be stood up through late 2026 and 2027, and its cost will land in selling expense before any of its retail margin lands in gross profit, so the reported numbers get worse before they get better even if the strategy is right. Meanwhile the cost driver is still running: with producer prices at 5.4% and import prices up 7.0% year on year, and central banks tightening rather than easing, the commodity inflation that took 4.7 points off gross margin is being reinforced by the macro backdrop rather than relieved by it. The first quarter of each year is also this company's cash-flow trough, as supplier float unwinds after the year-end push, so a weak first quarter of 2027 should be expected and will look alarming.
positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure has been severe and is probably not finished. The Hong Kong listing came on 5 November 2025 at HK$131.5, valuing the company near CNY 196 billion against CNY 165 billion of revenue, roughly 1.2 times revenue for a vehicle assembler at a moment when the closest comparables traded near 0.55 to 0.65 times. The shares are now 73% below that price and sit 2% off the bottom of their 52-week range, 53% below the 200-day average. A large part of that decline is the deflation of a badly priced offering rather than new information, and every investor who bought the deal is deeply under water. The mechanics make it worse: the Hong Kong line is only about 109 million of the 1.742 billion shares outstanding, roughly 6% of the company, so it is thin, and thin lines overshoot in both directions. The gap to the Shanghai A-shares has widened to about 37%, and there is no conversion mechanism between the two classes that would force it shut. Institutional interest is negligible, with a smart-money score of 5 out of 100. The washout is real; what is not yet visible is evidence that it has finished.
moderator_conclusion: Wait for the wash-out. This is a genuinely cheap asset with a genuinely weakened competitive position, and the two facts do not cancel out. The case for patience rather than a pass is that the damage in the first half of 2026 was to price and cost, not to demand: the company sold 196,580 vehicles, down barely 1%, and electric units grew, while gross margin fell 4.7 points to 21.8% on a 132.2% rise in lithium carbonate prices and a chip shortage. Strip the CNY 1.75 billion non-cash write-down and the CNY 1.72 billion loss is a modest operating stumble, not a broken business. Against that, the case for not buying yet is stronger and rests on three things. First, on 15 September 2026 Huawei handed back product definition, design, brand marketing and retail channels for AITO while keeping operational leadership of its four other alliance brands; whatever else that is, it is the partner de-prioritising this brand, and Seres must now fund a national retail network from a standing start while volumes fall. Second, the cheapness is almost entirely a balance-sheet add-back rather than an earnings discount. Value the whole company on revenue with no cash credit and the Hong Kong line sits at about 0.33 times against 0.65 times for Li Auto and 0.55 times for Leapmotor, a real but ordinary discount; the dramatic version only appears once you credit a cash pile that is financed by CNY 38.8 billion of supplier notes and that ran backwards by CNY 20.95 billion in a single quarter. Third, the driver that broke the margin is commodity inflation, and with producer prices at 5.4%, import prices up 7.0%, and the Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan all hiking in the nine days to 18 September, the macro backdrop is reinforcing that pressure rather than relieving it. A recovery thesis here is partly a bet on lithium rolling over, which is one shared factor doing too much work. We judge the fair value of the Hong Kong line at HK$46.50, about 32% above the HK$35.14 price, against an adverse case of HK$23.50 about 33% below it. That is a coin flip dressed as a bargain, and the resolution point is five weeks away in the third-quarter report. The right action is to carry this as a watched name, not an owned one, and to revisit it on a print that shows gross margin recovering and cash flow turning positive. On the value case judged alone, without any credit or penalty for the catalyst and ignoring the macro tilt, this rates a three: the discount to the parts is real and the Yinwang stake gets no recognition, but returns on invested capital of 0.7%, a write-down of capitalised development spending, five new ventures launched in five months while the core brand shrank, and a moat that was rented from Huawei and is now being handed back all cap how far that case can be pushed. An eroding moat is not something a low multiple compensates for.
sop_fair_value: Base case HK$46.50 a share, about 32% above the HK$35.14 price on 22 September 2026, over an eighteen-month horizon. The reconciliation sits closer to the adverse case than to the favorable one, for one reason: almost all of the apparent cheapness is a balance-sheet add-back rather than an earnings discount, and the balance sheet does not support the company's own framing of it.
sop_breakdown: All figures in Chinese yuan across 1.742 billion shares, then converted to the Hong Kong line at HK$1 = CNY 0.85477. Vehicle business: CNY 160 billion of revenue, roughly flat with 2025 and slightly below the CNY 159.3 billion analyst consensus for 2026, at 0.32 times enterprise value to revenue, which is half of Li Auto's 0.65 times and well under Leapmotor's 0.55 times. That deliberate halving prices in the loss of Huawei's retail channel and the cost of rebuilding one. Value CNY 51.2 billion, or CNY 29.39 a share. Yinwang 10% stake: carried at CNY 13.5 billion, CNY 7.75 a share. Net cash: CNY 22 billion, CNY 12.63 a share. This is the CNY 73.13 billion of cash and short-term investments less CNY 4.35 billion of genuine borrowing and less the CNY 38.8 billion of supplier notes, which gives CNY 30 billion, then haircut by about a quarter for the portion of the float that a shrinking business consumes rather than releases. New ventures: zero, on the view that their option value and their cash burn offset. The parts sum to CNY 86.7 billion, or CNY 49.77 a share. That figure lands almost exactly on where the Shanghai A-shares trade today at CNY 47.78, which is a useful check rather than a coincidence: the domestic market is pricing this business roughly where the parts say it belongs. The Hong Kong line then carries a 20% listing discount, narrower than today's 37% gap but not closed, because a Hong Kong share of a Chinese issuer cannot be converted into a domestic share and there is no mechanism that forces the gap shut. That gives CNY 39.8, or HK$46.50. risk_reward: Roughly balanced, which is the honest answer and not an attractive one. From HK$35.14, the base case at HK$46.50 offers about 32% of upside and the adverse case at HK$23.50 about 33% of downside, over eighteen months. The favorable case at HK$97 is real but requires three separate things to go right at once. What makes this setup uncomfortable is not the ratio but the shape of the distribution. The upside is concentrated in two numbers an investor cannot verify from outside: how much of the CNY 73 billion cash pile is genuinely spare rather than supplier credit, and what the independent AITO sales network will cost to build. The downside, by contrast, is driven by things already visible in the filings. There is also no structural floor beneath the shares. Net cash per share of CNY 17.2, or about HK$20, looks like one, but a cash balance that moved by CNY 21 billion on working-capital timing in a single quarter is not a floor, and I have deliberately recorded no floor price for this name. catalyst_status_plain: a soft catalyst, no fixed date
peer_comps_note: Our stored peer file for this name is unmapped and carries no comparable set, so the peer group was rebuilt from live market data on 22 September 2026 rather than from memory.
