interrogator_dossier:
# Forensic Dossier — Seres Group Co., Ltd (9927.HK / 601127.SS)

**Date of review:** 2026-09-22 · **Price used:** HK$35.14 (Hong Kong listing, HKD) · **Shanghai A-line:** CNY 47.78

**A note on sources before anything else.** No earnings-call transcript exists for this company in our licensed data feed, and Chinese A-share issuers with a Hong Kong secondary listing do not hold the quarterly analyst calls that American companies do. There is therefore no multi-quarter transcript arc to read. Everything below is built from the company's own filed numbers (eight quarters of income statement, balance sheet and cash flow), its 12 July 2026 profit warning, its 19 August 2026 half-year report, and dated trade-press coverage of the Huawei partnership. Where I quote, I quote the filed half-year report as relayed by CnEVPost on 19 August 2026. I have invented nothing, and where a fact could not be verified I say so.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Seres makes the AITO (Wenjie) range of premium electric and range-extended sport-utility vehicles in Chongqing. It is not really an ordinary carmaker. Until one week ago it was the manufacturing half of a partnership in which Huawei did almost everything that touches the customer — defined the product, designed the vehicle, built the brand, and sold the cars through its own retail network — while Seres built them. That arrangement is what turned a loss-making minivan maker into a company with CNY 165 billion of revenue.

The arc across the last three years is one of the steepest in the industry, in both directions.

**2021 to 2023 — the pre-Huawei company.** Revenue of CNY 16.7 billion in 2021 rising to CNY 35.8 billion in 2023, with losses every year: CNY 1.82 billion, CNY 3.83 billion, CNY 2.45 billion. This was a subscale manufacturer going nowhere.

**2024 to 2025 — the Huawei years.** Revenue quadrupled to CNY 145.2 billion in 2024 and CNY 165.1 billion in 2025, and the company made money for the first time: CNY 5.95 billion and CNY 5.96 billion of net income. Gross margin reached 29.1% in 2025 — extraordinary for a volume carmaker and a direct product of Huawei's brand pricing power. Management spent heavily to secure the relationship: CNY 2.5 billion in July 2024 for the AITO trademarks and design patents, and CNY 11.5 billion in August 2024 for a 10% stake in Shenzhen Yinwang, Huawei's intelligent-automotive unit (the deal completed in September 2025). On 5 November 2025 the company listed in Hong Kong at HK$131.5 a share, raising roughly CNY 12.9 billion.

**2026 — the unwind.** The story since has contracted on every axis. First-half revenue fell 7.87% to CNY 57.49 billion, gross margin fell 4.7 percentage points to 21.8%, and the company swung to a net loss of CNY 1.72 billion from a CNY 2.94 billion profit a year earlier. In June the company cut the entry price of the new M6 by CNY 50,000, from CNY 279,800 to CNY 229,800 — an 18% cut on the trim that sets the brand's price floor. Then on 15 September 2026 Huawei handed operational control of AITO back to Seres: product definition, vehicle design, brand marketing, retail channels and service operations all transfer. AITO stays inside Huawei's HIMA alliance and keeps buying Huawei's driving software, but Seres must now build and fund its own sales network.

**What was quietly added.** While the core brand was shrinking, 2026 saw a remarkable burst of new initiatives: a premium-charging joint venture with BMW and Mercedes (17 April), a new vehicle brand connected to ByteDance (3 June), a second new brand called Aiva through affiliate Saidou (9 June), a humanoid robot (15 June), and a United Arab Emirates dealership (6 February). Five new directions in five months, from a company whose one profitable product line was losing share.

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

The company's explanation for the half-year loss is specific and testable. It blames input costs — battery-grade lithium carbonate up 132.2% year on year on an average daily price basis, plus "structural shortages and sharp price increases" in automotive-grade chips — and says it chose not to pass those costs to customers. It also took a CNY 1.75 billion write-down of intangible assets, attributed to "rapid technological iteration in the NEV industry."

| Management's claim | What the filed numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| The problem is input costs, not demand | Unit sales were 196,580, down only 1.02%; electric-vehicle units actually rose 3.87% to 178,777. Revenue fell 7.87%, so the average selling price fell about 7%. Gross margin fell 4.7 points. | **Largely supported.** Volume held; price and cost did the damage. This is genuinely a margin event, not a demand collapse. |
| "We declined to pass these costs to customers" | True in the sense that prices were not raised — but the company went the other way and *cut* the M6 entry price by CNY 50,000 in June. | **Poorer than the story.** This is not restraint; it is the absence of pricing power, described kindly. |
| Scale is still building | Half-year revenue of CNY 57.49 billion is below the CNY 62.40 billion of a year earlier; the second half of 2025 alone did CNY 102.6 billion. The business is running below its own recent peak. | **Diverges.** |
| The write-down reflects industry pace | The CNY 1.75 billion charge sits against CNY 12.3 billion of intangible assets carried on the balance sheet, much of it capitalised development spending. Writing off capitalised development because technology moved on is the textbook sign that the spending was capitalised too aggressively in the first place. | **Concerning.** The charge is honest; what it reveals about the earlier accounting is not flattering. |
| The balance sheet is a fortress — cash above CNY 73.15 billion, 57% of total assets, with interest-bearing debt only 3.2% of assets | Both figures are accurate. But the cash is funded by supplier credit: CNY 38.8 billion of notes payable to suppliers plus CNY 19.9 billion of trade payables. Net working capital is only CNY 3.84 billion. The company collects from customers in about 8 days and pays suppliers in about 61. | **Accurate but seriously misleading if read as spare cash.** See section 6. |

**The single most important forensic finding in this file** concerns that cash. In the first quarter of 2026, operating cash flow was *minus CNY 20.95 billion* in three months — the supplier float draining after the year-end volume push. The second quarter put CNY 8.47 billion back. Across the half, operating cash flow was minus CNY 12.38 billion. A cash balance that swings by twenty billion on working-capital timing is not a store of value the way an investor instinctively reads "57% of assets are cash." It is the float of a business that is paid instantly and pays late, and it shrinks when volumes shrink.

**Two numbers in our own screener file are wrong and must not be used.** The scan reports price-to-free-cash-flow of 2.0x and a discounted-cash-flow fair value of 198.1 — both computed from the 2025 peak-year cash flow. On a trailing twelve-month basis free cash flow is *minus* CNY 3.27 billion. The screener's net-debt field is also wrong; the corrected balance-sheet figure is in section 6.

---

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rating: Declining**, judged from disclosure behaviour rather than call transcripts, since none exist.

The sequence is telling. On **12 July 2026** the company issued a profit warning flagging a half-year net loss of CNY 1.5 billion to CNY 1.8 billion and naming the causes as rising material costs and asset write-downs. On **19 August 2026** it reported a loss of CNY 1.72 billion — inside its own range, and close to the middle of it. That is competent, unpanicked disclosure and it deserves credit.

But the *content* of the disclosure has shifted from offensive to defensive in one year. The 2025 language was about scale, premium positioning and a 29% gross margin. The 2026 language is about lithium prices, chip shortages, write-downs and "maintaining premium supply standards" — the vocabulary of a management team explaining a result rather than setting a direction. Research and development spending rose 27.4% to CNY 3.73 billion into a shrinking revenue base, which reads as commitment rather than retreat; but it sits alongside five new ventures launched in five months, which reads as a company casting about for the next story because the current one has stopped working.

---

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Score: Medium.**

The evidence that exists is good. The July warning was issued roughly five weeks before the result, gave a numerical range, named the causes, and the reported figure landed inside it. Chinese issuers are required to warn on large swings, so this is compliance rather than virtue — but plenty of companies warn late, warn vaguely, or warn low and then miss their own range. Seres did none of those.

Against that, the screener's earnings-beat record is 2 of the last 4 quarters, a 50% hit rate, which is coin-flip. And there is a structural pattern the director should hold in mind: this company's results are extremely back-half-weighted. The first half of 2025 was CNY 62.4 billion of revenue against CNY 102.6 billion in the second half. The same shape is embedded in the current consensus, which expects CNY 159.3 billion for full-year 2026 against CNY 57.5 billion delivered in the first half — implying a second half of roughly CNY 102 billion, essentially matching the prior year's record second half at a moment when the brand is losing share. That is a demanding number and it has not been de-risked.

---

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

With no calls, the pressure points must be inferred from what the company does and does not quantify. Three stand out.

**The Huawei dependency was never quantified, and now it is changing.** Seres has never disclosed what it pays Huawei — for the driving software, for the retail channel, for the brand. The 15 September restructuring changes all of those economics at once, and the company disclosed no new fee or equity arrangement alongside it. An investor is being asked to underwrite a transition whose cost is undisclosed.

**AITO's own volumes are not broken out.** The company reports total units. The alliance-level data that is public tells an uncomfortable story: Huawei's HIMA alliance delivered about 192,000 units from January to May 2026, up 26.5% year on year, while Seres's revenue fell 8% over the half. The alliance is growing; Seres's share of it is not. In August, HIMA deliveries themselves turned negative, down 5.52% year on year.

**Nobody has been made to explain the working-capital swing.** A negative CNY 20.95 billion operating quarter in a company that headlines its cash position is the question I would ask first, and there is no public forum in which it has been asked.

There is a further gap worth stating plainly: I could find no dated analyst price target for the Hong Kong line. Our data provider has no price-target coverage for this listing, and the web-search budget for this session was exhausted before a broker target could be sourced. I therefore use no target figure anywhere in this file.

---

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 **The cash is supplier float, not a war chest.** Cash and short-term investments of CNY 73.13 billion are financed by CNY 38.8 billion of supplier notes and CNY 19.9 billion of trade payables. Netting the supplier notes and the CNY 4.35 billion of genuine borrowings leaves roughly **CNY 30 billion of defensible net cash** — about CNY 17.2 a share, or HK$20.1. The company's own framing (debt is 3.2% of assets) implies nearly CNY 69 billion, which would be more than the entire Hong Kong-line market value. I do not accept that framing, and the first quarter's cash flow is the reason.

🔴 **Returns on capital have gone to nothing.** Trailing return on equity is 3.6% and return on invested capital 0.7%. The screener's full-year figures are worse still. A company earning less on its capital than it can earn on a bank deposit is not compounding.

🔴 **Capitalised development spending written off.** CNY 1.75 billion of intangibles impaired for "rapid technological iteration," against CNY 12.3 billion still carried. A further CNY 2.31 billion sits in "other gains and losses."

🔴 **The partner stepped back from this brand and only this brand.** Huawei retains operational leadership of the other four HIMA marques — Luxeed, Stelato, Maextro and Shangjie. It handed back the one it had built first. That ordering matters.

🔴 **Five new ventures in five months** while the core brand shrank: a charging joint venture, a ByteDance-linked brand, the Aiva brand, a humanoid robot, a Gulf dealership. Each is a call on management attention and capital.

🔴 **The listing itself was sold at a peak.** The November 2025 initial public offering priced at HK$131.5, valuing the whole company near CNY 196 billion on CNY 165 billion of revenue — roughly 1.2x revenue for a vehicle assembler, when the closest listed comparables trade around 0.55x to 0.65x. Much of the 73% decline since is the deflation of that price, not new information.

🟢 **Volume held.** Units fell only 1.02% and electric units rose 3.87%. The franchise did not lose its customers; it lost its price.

🟢 **The loss is smaller than it looks.** Strip the CNY 1.75 billion write-down and the half-year result is an operating stumble of a few percent on CNY 57.5 billion of revenue, not a structural cash loss.

🟢 **Seres now owns the customer.** Whatever the execution risk, product definition, design, brand and retail all move in-house from 15 September. The retail margin Huawei captured is now Seres's to capture — and Seres already owns the AITO trademarks outright.

🟢 **A real, under-recognised financial asset.** The 10% stake in Huawei's Yinwang unit, bought for CNY 11.5 billion and carried at about CNY 13.5 billion, is a minority interest in the supplier of driving software to the entire HIMA alliance and to third parties. It earns no line in the income statement that an investor would notice.

🟢 **Honest pre-announcement.** The July warning was specific, early and accurate.

---

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

**The language of the 15 September announcement is the signal.** Huawei transferred "product definition, product design, brand marketing, retail channels and service operations." That is not a delegation of tasks; it is the return of an entire commercial function. Read one way it is a promotion — Seres graduates from contract manufacturer to brand owner. Read the other way, the party that made the brand work has decided its time is better spent on four other brands, and the manufacturer now has to reproduce Huawei's retail machine from a standing start, with falling volumes, in a price war. Both readings are available from the same sentence. The second is the one the share price is pricing.

**The sequencing of the write-down.** The impairment of capitalised development landed in the same half as the loss of product-definition authority. Intangible assets are written down when the cash flows behind them shrink. It is hard not to read the charge as an early, quiet acknowledgement of the September change.

**A tell in the working capital.** Days of payables outstanding is about 61 against 8 days of receivables and 7 days of inventory — a cash conversion cycle of minus 47 days. That is a supplier-financed model. It works beautifully at scale and reverses violently on the way down, which is exactly what the first quarter showed.

**A new voice, and what it is selling.** The 2026 initiative list — robotics, an internet-company car brand, a charging network with German luxury marques — is the vocabulary of a company that wants to be valued as a technology platform rather than an assembler. That ambition is not yet visible anywhere in the returns on capital.

---

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: DETERIORATING**, with a genuine restructuring underway that could change the label but has not yet.

Revenue is down 8%, gross margin down 4.7 points, the company has swung to a loss, operating cash flow ran minus CNY 12.38 billion in the half, and the brand is losing share inside an alliance that is growing. The Huawei handover is a real pivot and may prove to be the right one, but it is one week old and entirely unproven.

**The single thing the director must weigh before sizing this:** almost all of the apparent cheapness is a balance-sheet add-back, not an earnings discount. Value the whole company on revenue with no cash credit and the Hong Kong line trades at roughly 0.33x revenue against 0.65x for Li Auto and 0.55x for Leapmotor — a discount, but a defensible one for a brand losing relative share. Credit the CNY 30 billion of net cash and the operating business is being valued at almost nothing. The entire investment case turns on whether that cash is spare or is supplier float that a volume decline would consume. On the first quarter's evidence, it is a great deal more float than spare. Size the position to the version of the balance sheet you actually believe, not the version the company presents.

**Economic moat.** The moat here was never Seres's. It was Huawei's brand, Huawei's driving software and Huawei's retail network, rented to a manufacturer that supplied the factory. The type is best described as intangible-brand and channel access, held on loan. The evidence says it is narrowing on every measure the returns provide: gross margin from 29.1% in 2025 to 21.8% in the first half of 2026, return on invested capital down to 0.7%, pricing cut by CNY 50,000 on the entry trim, and the brand shrinking while its own alliance grew 26.5% through May. By the returns-and-margin test this is an eroding moat, not a wide one, and the 15 September transfer of channel and brand authority is the formal confirmation of that erosion rather than a cure for it.

**Terminal value.** The threat is real but not terminal. China's electric-vehicle market is growing, not shrinking, so this is not a melting base. The structural risk is different: in a vehicle built around someone else's driving software and sold through someone else's shops, the durable economics accrue to the software and channel owner, and the assembler is commoditised. Seres has partially hedged that — it owns 10% of Yinwang and it owns the AITO marks — but it has not escaped it. I judge the secular threat **material, not terminal**, and note that none of the eight named structural forces in our own controlled vocabulary describes this risk; forcing one on would be false precision.

**Fear-print or value trap?** Neither cleanly. It is a genuine de-rating from a genuinely absurd listing price, on top of a real margin shock, in a business whose competitive position got weaker in the same quarter. The cheapness is real on a revenue basis and overstated on a cash basis. That combination argues for patience and a small size, not for conviction in either direction.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a moat that is being eroded · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.

bull_thesis: Seres builds the AITO range of premium electric and range-extended sport-utility vehicles in Chongqing, and the bull case rests on a simple observation: what broke in 2026 was the price of the cars, not the demand for them. In the first half of 2026 the company sold 196,580 vehicles, down just 1.02% from a year earlier, and electric units actually rose 3.87% to 178,777. Revenue fell 7.87% to CNY 57.49 billion and gross margin fell 4.7 percentage points to 21.8%, which means almost all of the damage came from price and input cost rather than from customers walking away. Management named the culprits precisely in the 19 August 2026 half-year report: the average daily price of battery-grade lithium carbonate rose 132.2% year on year, and automotive-grade chips ran into what the company called structural shortages and sharp price increases. Those are cyclical commodity inputs, not a broken franchise. Strip out the CNY 1.75 billion non-cash write-down of intangible assets and the CNY 1.72 billion reported loss becomes a few percentage points of operating slippage on a CNY 57.5 billion revenue base. The second leg of the case is the 15 September 2026 restructuring of the Huawei relationship. Huawei handed Seres operational control of AITO, transferring product definition, vehicle design, brand marketing, retail channels and service operations, while AITO stays inside Huawei's HIMA alliance and keeps buying Huawei's driving software. Seres already bought the AITO trademarks and design patents outright for CNY 2.5 billion in July 2024. The optimistic reading is that a company that was paid only to manufacture now owns the customer relationship and the retail margin that went with it, for the first time. The third leg is the balance sheet. The company holds CNY 73.13 billion of cash and short-term investments against roughly CNY 4.35 billion of genuine interest-bearing borrowing, and it owns 10% of Shenzhen Yinwang, Huawei's intelligent-automotive unit, bought for CNY 11.5 billion in August 2024 and carried at about CNY 13.5 billion. Yinwang supplies driving software to every brand in the alliance and to outside customers, and that stake earns no line in Seres's profit that an investor would notice. Finally, the starting point is unusually low. The Hong Kong line at HK$35.14 values the entire company, all 1.742 billion shares, at about CNY 52 billion against roughly CNY 160 billion of revenue. Analyst consensus has 2026 as the trough at CNY 0.44 of earnings per share and 2027 at CNY 3.05, which would put the Hong Kong line under 10 times forward earnings before any credit for cash. For this case to work, three things must hold: lithium and chip costs must stop rising, the independent AITO sales network must be built without a second year of margin destruction, and the second half of 2026 must deliver the sharp seasonal recovery both 2024 and 2025 produced. Since the last look the bull case gained two pieces of support. On 30 September 2026 Huawei and Seres signed a new five-year agreement that keeps AITO inside the alliance with continued Huawei technology support and a jointly built AITO team, which argues the 15 September handover was a division of labour rather than an exit. And the same day the refreshed M8 opened pre-sales CNY 30,000 above its predecessor at CNY 389,800, the first sign this year that the brand can push price rather than cut it.
bear_thesis: The bear case is that the one thing that made Seres valuable has just been handed back to it, and the cheapness that makes the shares look compelling is an accounting illusion. Start with the partnership. Huawei did not merely manufacture a change of administration on 15 September 2026; it withdrew from the brand it built first while retaining operational leadership of the four other alliance marques, Luxeed, Stelato, Maextro and Shangjie. The ordering is the message. Huawei's product definition, brand marketing and retail network were the moat, rented rather than owned, and Seres must now reproduce a national retail machine from a standing start, while volumes fall and a price war runs. That build is a fixed-cost commitment landing on a business whose selling and administrative expense already ran CNY 5.37 billion in the second quarter alone, seventeen percent of revenue. The competitive evidence is already visible. Huawei's HIMA alliance delivered about 192,000 units from January to May 2026, up 26.5% year on year, while Seres's own revenue fell about 8% across the half. The alliance grew; AITO's share of it shrank. By August, alliance deliveries themselves turned negative, down 5.52% year on year. Seres cut the entry price of the M6 by CNY 50,000, from CNY 279,800 to CNY 229,800, in June 2026, an 18% cut on the trim that anchors the range. Management describes its decision not to raise prices as a choice to maintain premium supply standards; the filed numbers describe a company with no pricing power cutting into a cost shock. Then the balance sheet, which is where the real risk sits. The company presents cash above CNY 73.15 billion as 57% of total assets with interest-bearing debt at only 3.2% of assets. Both figures are true and both are misleading. That cash is financed by CNY 38.8 billion of notes payable to suppliers and CNY 19.9 billion of trade payables. Net working capital is CNY 3.84 billion. The company collects from customers in roughly 8 days and pays suppliers in roughly 61, a cash conversion cycle of minus 47 days, and in the first quarter of 2026 that float ran backwards: operating cash flow was minus CNY 20.95 billion in three months, and minus CNY 12.38 billion across the half. Trailing free cash flow is minus CNY 3.27 billion. A cash pile that moves twenty billion on working-capital timing is not a floor under the share price; it is a liability that happens to sit on the asset side. Quality is thin elsewhere too. Trailing return on invested capital is 0.7% and return on equity 3.6%. The company wrote off CNY 1.75 billion of capitalised development spending for rapid technological iteration, against CNY 12.3 billion still carried, with a further CNY 2.31 billion of other losses. And while the core brand shrank, management launched five new ventures in five months: a charging joint venture with BMW and Mercedes in April, a ByteDance-linked vehicle brand in June, the Aiva brand in June, a humanoid robot in June, and a Gulf dealership in February. That is attention and capital leaving the one business that works. Finally, the consensus that makes the shares look cheap is itself demanding: full-year 2026 revenue of CNY 159.3 billion against CNY 57.5 billion delivered in the first half implies a second half of roughly CNY 102 billion, matching the record second half of 2025 at the exact moment the brand is losing relative share. Confirmation of the bear case would be a third-quarter print in late October showing gross margin still near 21%, a second consecutive quarter of negative operating cash flow, or disclosed spending on the new sales network that exceeds the retail margin it is meant to capture. The newest data point supports the bear: on 1 October 2026 the Huawei alliance reported September deliveries of 37,490, down 29.15% year on year and down 10.95% from August, its fourth straight year-on-year decline, in the last month of the quarter the October report will cover. The new five-year Huawei agreement disclosed no financial terms, so the cost of the relationship, previously about 10% of each vehicle's price in fees on CNY 56.05 billion of 2025 purchases from Huawei, remains unknowable from outside. And the M8 price rise is partly bought with extra content, so it does not by itself prove pricing power.
consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market is narrower than the 73% share-price decline would suggest, and it runs in both directions. The market appears to be treating this as a demand collapse. It is not: first-half 2026 unit sales fell only 1.02% and electric units rose 3.87%, so the franchise kept its customers and lost its price. On that point we are more positive than the tape. But we are markedly more negative than the company's own presentation of its balance sheet. Management frames cash above CNY 73.15 billion, 57% of total assets, against interest-bearing debt of only 3.2% of assets, which implies nearly CNY 69 billion of net cash, more than the entire Hong Kong-line market value. We treat the CNY 38.8 billion of notes payable to suppliers as debt, which cuts defensible net cash to about CNY 30 billion, and then haircut that again for the float a shrinking business consumes. The first quarter of 2026 settles the argument: operating cash flow of minus CNY 20.95 billion in three months is not what a fortress balance sheet does. Our second disagreement is with the sell side on 2027. Consensus of CNY 3.05 of earnings per share requires both a margin recovery and a volume recovery in a brand whose partner has just stepped back and which must fund a new retail network; we underwrite the revenue but not the multiple that number would normally earn.
forcing_function: There is no single event that forces a re-rating, which remains the central weakness of the setup. The closest is the third-quarter report due in late October 2026: gross margin back above 24%, positive operating cash flow, and a disclosed cost for the new sales network and the new five-year Huawei arrangement together would be the proof that the margin shock was cyclical and the handover a promotion rather than a demotion. Any two of those would justify revisiting at a larger size. The 30 September 2026 five-year Huawei agreement and the M8 refresh priced CNY 30,000 higher are helpful but have already been announced, and the weak September alliance deliveries make a strong third-quarter print less likely, not more. Beyond the report, the real forcing function is commodity rather than corporate, lithium prices rolling over, which is a single shared factor across the whole sector and gets no credit here.
valley_of_death: The risky window is the next two to three quarters, and it now has a first data point. Third-quarter results land in late October 2026 and will show whether the seasonal second-half recovery that carried 2024 and 2025 is intact. The early read is poor: the Huawei alliance delivered 37,490 vehicles in September 2026, down 29.15% year on year and 10.95% below August. Consensus needs a second half of roughly CNY 102 billion of revenue against CNY 57.5 billion in the first half, matching the record second half of 2025; if it does not arrive, the full-year 2026 earnings estimate of CNY 0.44 a share goes first and the 2027 recovery number second. The cost of the self-run sales network will land in selling expense before its retail margin lands in gross profit, and the undisclosed economics of the new five-year Huawei agreement add a second unknown to the cost line. The macro backdrop is not helping: producer prices are running 5.4% year on year and the Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan all raised rates in September, so the input inflation that took 4.7 points off gross margin is being reinforced rather than relieved. The first quarter of each year is also this company's cash-flow trough as supplier credit unwinds after the year-end push, so an alarming-looking first quarter of 2027 should be expected.
positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure has been severe and is probably not finished. The Hong Kong listing came on 5 November 2025 at HK$131.5, valuing the company near CNY 196 billion against CNY 165 billion of revenue, roughly 1.2 times revenue for a vehicle assembler at a moment when the closest comparables traded near 0.55 to 0.65 times. At HK$36.48 on 5 October 2026 the shares are about 72% below that price, roughly 15% above the HK$31.64 52-week low, and about 48% below the 200-day average of roughly HK$70. A large part of that decline is the deflation of a badly priced offering rather than new information, and every investor who bought the deal is deeply under water. The mechanics make it worse: the Hong Kong line is only about 109 million of the 1.742 billion shares outstanding, roughly 6% of the company, so it is thin, and thin lines overshoot in both directions. The gap to the Shanghai A-shares has widened to about 37%, and there is no conversion mechanism between the two classes that would force it shut. Institutional interest is negligible, with a smart-money score of 5 out of 100. The washout is real; what is not yet visible is evidence that it has finished.
moderator_conclusion: Wait for the wash-out, unchanged from the 22 September 2026 review. This is a genuinely cheap asset with a genuinely weakened competitive position, and the two facts do not cancel out. The damage in the first half of 2026 was to price and cost rather than demand: 196,580 vehicles sold, down barely 1%, while gross margin fell 4.7 points to 21.8% on a 132.2% rise in lithium carbonate prices and a chip shortage. Against buying now: the cheapness is almost entirely a balance-sheet add-back rather than an earnings discount, since valued on revenue with no cash credit the Hong Kong line sits at about 0.34 times against 0.65 times for Li Auto and 0.55 times for Leapmotor, and the cash pile it relies on is financed by CNY 38.8 billion of supplier notes and ran backwards by CNY 20.95 billion in a single quarter; returns on invested capital are 0.7%; and the margin recovery is partly a bet on lithium prices, one shared factor doing too much work while three major central banks have just raised rates against inflation. The 30 September 2026 five-year Huawei agreement takes the worst reading of the September handover off the table, Huawei is staying for five years, but discloses no terms. The refreshed M8 priced CNY 30,000 higher is the first pricing signal of the year, partly bought with extra content. And the alliance's September deliveries, down 29.15% year on year, point to a soft third quarter just as the company needs a record second half. On the value case alone, ignoring catalysts and the macro tilt, this remains a three: the discount to the parts is real and the Yinwang stake is unrecognised, but very low returns, a write-down of capitalised development, a scatter of new ventures, and a moat rented from a partner whose new terms are undisclosed cap how far that case can be pushed.

# Forensic Dossier — Seres Group Co., Ltd (9927.HK / 601127.SS)

**Date of review:** 2026-10-05 (continuing coverage; full prior review 2026-09-22) · **Price used:** HK$36.48 (Hong Kong listing 9927.HK, HKD, live quote 2026-10-05) · Figures in Chinese yuan (CNY) unless stated

**What changed since the last look (dated, 23 September to 5 October 2026).** Three facts are new, and they pull in opposite directions:

1. **30 September 2026 — a new five-year agreement with Huawei** (announced 1 October, reported by CnEVPost). This narrows the worst reading of the 15 September handover: Huawei is not walking away from the brand for at least five years. It does not answer the question that matters for value, which is what the new arrangement costs.

A price increase is the first pricing-power signal in 2026 after the CNY 50,000 cut to the M6 entry trim in June; it is partly paid for by more content (Huawei's latest driver-assistance system across the range), so it is not a clean like-for-like price rise.
3. **1 October 2026 — HIMA alliance September deliveries of 37,490 vehicles, down 29.15% year on year and 10.95% month on month**, the alliance's fourth straight year-on-year decline; year-to-date deliveries are still up 5.27% at 367,229. Trade press attributes part of the drop to model changeovers. Seres's own September figure was not available to me at the time of writing (my web-search budget for this session was exhausted; CnEVPost's September roundup does not break out Seres). For a business whose consensus needs a record-matching second half, an alliance down 29% in the last month of the third quarter is the wrong direction.

Net effect: one tail risk narrowed (partner exit), one small positive pricing signal, one near-term negative volume signal. None of it changes the assessment below, which is carried forward from the 22 September review with these facts added.

**A note on sources before anything else.** No earnings-call transcript exists for this company in our licensed data feed, and Chinese A-share issuers with a Hong Kong secondary listing do not hold the quarterly analyst calls that American companies do. There is therefore no multi-quarter transcript arc to read. Everything below is built from the company's own filed numbers (eight quarters of income statement, balance sheet and cash flow), its 12 July 2026 profit warning, its 19 August 2026 half-year report, and dated trade-press coverage of the Huawei partnership. Where I quote, I quote the filed half-year report as relayed by CnEVPost on 19 August 2026. I have invented nothing, and where a fact could not be verified I say so.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Seres makes the AITO (Wenjie) range of premium electric and range-extended sport-utility vehicles in Chongqing. It is not really an ordinary carmaker. Until one week ago it was the manufacturing half of a partnership in which Huawei did almost everything that touches the customer — defined the product, designed the vehicle, built the brand, and sold the cars through its own retail network — while Seres built them. That arrangement is what turned a loss-making minivan maker into a company with CNY 165 billion of revenue.

The arc across the last three years is one of the steepest in the industry, in both directions.

**2021 to 2023 — the pre-Huawei company.** Revenue of CNY 16.7 billion in 2021 rising to CNY 35.8 billion in 2023, with losses every year: CNY 1.82 billion, CNY 3.83 billion, CNY 2.45 billion. This was a subscale manufacturer going nowhere.

**2024 to 2025 — the Huawei years.** Revenue quadrupled to CNY 145.2 billion in 2024 and CNY 165.1 billion in 2025, and the company made money for the first time: CNY 5.95 billion and CNY 5.96 billion of net income. Gross margin reached 29.1% in 2025 — extraordinary for a volume carmaker and a direct product of Huawei's brand pricing power. Management spent heavily to secure the relationship: CNY 2.5 billion in July 2024 for the AITO trademarks and design patents, and CNY 11.5 billion in August 2024 for a 10% stake in Shenzhen Yinwang, Huawei's intelligent-automotive unit (the deal completed in September 2025). On 5 November 2025 the company listed in Hong Kong at HK$131.5 a share, raising roughly CNY 12.9 billion.

**2026 — the unwind.** The story since has contracted on every axis. First-half revenue fell 7.87% to CNY 57.49 billion, gross margin fell 4.7 percentage points to 21.8%, and the company swung to a net loss of CNY 1.72 billion from a CNY 2.94 billion profit a year earlier. In June the company cut the entry price of the new M6 by CNY 50,000, from CNY 279,800 to CNY 229,800 — an 18% cut on the trim that sets the brand's price floor. Then on 15 September 2026 Huawei handed operational control of AITO back to Seres: product definition, vehicle design, brand marketing, retail channels and service operations all transfer. AITO stays inside Huawei's HIMA alliance and keeps buying Huawei's driving software, but Seres must now build and fund its own sales network.

**What was quietly added.** While the core brand was shrinking, 2026 saw a remarkable burst of new initiatives: a premium-charging joint venture with BMW and Mercedes (17 April), a new vehicle brand connected to ByteDance (3 June), a second new brand called Aiva through affiliate Saidou (9 June), a humanoid robot (15 June), and a United Arab Emirates dealership (6 February). Five new directions in five months, from a company whose one profitable product line was losing share.

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

The company's explanation for the half-year loss is specific and testable. It blames input costs — battery-grade lithium carbonate up 132.2% year on year on an average daily price basis, plus "structural shortages and sharp price increases" in automotive-grade chips — and says it chose not to pass those costs to customers. It also took a CNY 1.75 billion write-down of intangible assets, attributed to "rapid technological iteration in the NEV industry."

| Management's claim | What the filed numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| The problem is input costs, not demand | Unit sales were 196,580, down only 1.02%; electric-vehicle units actually rose 3.87% to 178,777. Revenue fell 7.87%, so the average selling price fell about 7%. Gross margin fell 4.7 points. | **Largely supported.** Volume held; price and cost did the damage. This is genuinely a margin event, not a demand collapse. |
| "We declined to pass these costs to customers" | True in the sense that prices were not raised — but the company went the other way and *cut* the M6 entry price by CNY 50,000 in June. | **Poorer than the story.** This is not restraint; it is the absence of pricing power, described kindly. |
| Scale is still building | Half-year revenue of CNY 57.49 billion is below the CNY 62.40 billion of a year earlier; the second half of 2025 alone did CNY 102.6 billion. The business is running below its own recent peak. | **Diverges.** |
| The write-down reflects industry pace | The CNY 1.75 billion charge sits against CNY 12.3 billion of intangible assets carried on the balance sheet, much of it capitalised development spending. Writing off capitalised development because technology moved on is the textbook sign that the spending was capitalised too aggressively in the first place. | **Concerning.** The charge is honest; what it reveals about the earlier accounting is not flattering. |
| The balance sheet is a fortress — cash above CNY 73.15 billion, 57% of total assets, with interest-bearing debt only 3.2% of assets | Both figures are accurate. But the cash is funded by supplier credit: CNY 38.8 billion of notes payable to suppliers plus CNY 19.9 billion of trade payables. Net working capital is only CNY 3.84 billion. The company collects from customers in about 8 days and pays suppliers in about 61. | **Accurate but seriously misleading if read as spare cash.** See section 6. |

**The single most important forensic finding in this file** concerns that cash. In the first quarter of 2026, operating cash flow was *minus CNY 20.95 billion* in three months — the supplier float draining after the year-end volume push. The second quarter put CNY 8.47 billion back. Across the half, operating cash flow was minus CNY 12.38 billion. A cash balance that swings by twenty billion on working-capital timing is not a store of value the way an investor instinctively reads "57% of assets are cash." It is the float of a business that is paid instantly and pays late, and it shrinks when volumes shrink.

**Two numbers in our own screener file are wrong and must not be used.** The scan reports price-to-free-cash-flow of 2.0x and a discounted-cash-flow fair value of 198.1 — both computed from the 2025 peak-year cash flow. On a trailing twelve-month basis free cash flow is *minus* CNY 3.27 billion. The screener's net-debt field is also wrong; the corrected balance-sheet figure is in section 6.

---

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rating: Declining**, judged from disclosure behaviour rather than call transcripts, since none exist.

The sequence is telling. On **12 July 2026** the company issued a profit warning flagging a half-year net loss of CNY 1.5 billion to CNY 1.8 billion and naming the causes as rising material costs and asset write-downs. On **19 August 2026** it reported a loss of CNY 1.72 billion — inside its own range, and close to the middle of it. That is competent, unpanicked disclosure and it deserves credit.

But the *content* of the disclosure has shifted from offensive to defensive in one year. The 2025 language was about scale, premium positioning and a 29% gross margin. The 2026 language is about lithium prices, chip shortages, write-downs and "maintaining premium supply standards" — the vocabulary of a management team explaining a result rather than setting a direction. Research and development spending rose 27.4% to CNY 3.73 billion into a shrinking revenue base, which reads as commitment rather than retreat; but it sits alongside five new ventures launched in five months, which reads as a company casting about for the next story because the current one has stopped working.

---

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Score: Medium.**

The evidence that exists is good. The July warning was issued roughly five weeks before the result, gave a numerical range, named the causes, and the reported figure landed inside it. Chinese issuers are required to warn on large swings, so this is compliance rather than virtue — but plenty of companies warn late, warn vaguely, or warn low and then miss their own range. Seres did none of those.

Against that, the screener's earnings-beat record is 2 of the last 4 quarters, a 50% hit rate, which is coin-flip. And there is a structural pattern the director should hold in mind: this company's results are extremely back-half-weighted. The first half of 2025 was CNY 62.4 billion of revenue against CNY 102.6 billion in the second half. The same shape is embedded in the current consensus, which expects CNY 159.3 billion for full-year 2026 against CNY 57.5 billion delivered in the first half — implying a second half of roughly CNY 102 billion, essentially matching the prior year's record second half at a moment when the brand is losing share. That is a demanding number and it has not been de-risked.

---

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

With no calls, the pressure points must be inferred from what the company does and does not quantify. Three stand out.

**The Huawei dependency was never quantified, and now it is changing.** Seres has never disclosed what it pays Huawei — for the driving software, for the retail channel, for the brand. The 15 September restructuring changes all of those economics at once, and the company disclosed no new fee or equity arrangement alongside it. An investor is being asked to underwrite a transition whose cost is undisclosed.

**AITO's own volumes are not broken out.** The company reports total units. The alliance-level data that is public tells an uncomfortable story: Huawei's HIMA alliance delivered about 192,000 units from January to May 2026, up 26.5% year on year, while Seres's revenue fell 8% over the half. The alliance is growing; Seres's share of it is not. In August, HIMA deliveries themselves turned negative, down 5.52% year on year.

**Nobody has been made to explain the working-capital swing.** A negative CNY 20.95 billion operating quarter in a company that headlines its cash position is the question I would ask first, and there is no public forum in which it has been asked.

There is a further gap worth stating plainly: I could find no dated analyst price target for the Hong Kong line. Our data provider has no price-target coverage for this listing, and the web-search budget for this session was exhausted before a broker target could be sourced. I therefore use no target figure anywhere in this file.

---

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 **The cash is supplier float, not a war chest.** Cash and short-term investments of CNY 73.13 billion are financed by CNY 38.8 billion of supplier notes and CNY 19.9 billion of trade payables. Netting the supplier notes and the CNY 4.35 billion of genuine borrowings leaves roughly **CNY 30 billion of defensible net cash** — about CNY 17.2 a share, or HK$20.1. The company's own framing (debt is 3.2% of assets) implies nearly CNY 69 billion, which would be more than the entire Hong Kong-line market value. I do not accept that framing, and the first quarter's cash flow is the reason.

🔴 **Returns on capital have gone to nothing.** Trailing return on equity is 3.6% and return on invested capital 0.7%. The screener's full-year figures are worse still. A company earning less on its capital than it can earn on a bank deposit is not compounding.

🔴 **Capitalised development spending written off.** CNY 1.75 billion of intangibles impaired for "rapid technological iteration," against CNY 12.3 billion still carried. A further CNY 2.31 billion sits in "other gains and losses."

🔴 **The partner stepped back from this brand and only this brand.** Huawei retains operational leadership of the other four HIMA marques — Luxeed, Stelato, Maextro and Shangjie. It handed back the one it had built first. That ordering matters.

🔴 **Five new ventures in five months** while the core brand shrank: a charging joint venture, a ByteDance-linked brand, the Aiva brand, a humanoid robot, a Gulf dealership. Each is a call on management attention and capital.

🔴 **The listing itself was sold at a peak.** The November 2025 initial public offering priced at HK$131.5, valuing the whole company near CNY 196 billion on CNY 165 billion of revenue — roughly 1.2x revenue for a vehicle assembler, when the closest listed comparables trade around 0.55x to 0.65x. Much of the 73% decline since is the deflation of that price, not new information.

🟢 **Volume held.** Units fell only 1.02% and electric units rose 3.87%. The franchise did not lose its customers; it lost its price.

🟢 **The loss is smaller than it looks.** Strip the CNY 1.75 billion write-down and the half-year result is an operating stumble of a few percent on CNY 57.5 billion of revenue, not a structural cash loss.

🟢 **Seres now owns the customer.** Whatever the execution risk, product definition, design, brand and retail all move in-house from 15 September. The retail margin Huawei captured is now Seres's to capture — and Seres already owns the AITO trademarks outright.

🟢 **A real, under-recognised financial asset.** The 10% stake in Huawei's Yinwang unit, bought for CNY 11.5 billion and carried at about CNY 13.5 billion, is a minority interest in the supplier of driving software to the entire HIMA alliance and to third parties. It earns no line in the income statement that an investor would notice.

🟢 **Honest pre-announcement.** The July warning was specific, early and accurate.

---

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

**The language of the 15 September announcement is the signal.** Huawei transferred "product definition, product design, brand marketing, retail channels and service operations." That is not a delegation of tasks; it is the return of an entire commercial function. Read one way it is a promotion — Seres graduates from contract manufacturer to brand owner. Read the other way, the party that made the brand work has decided its time is better spent on four other brands, and the manufacturer now has to reproduce Huawei's retail machine from a standing start, with falling volumes, in a price war. Both readings are available from the same sentence. The second is the one the share price is pricing.

**The sequencing of the write-down.** The impairment of capitalised development landed in the same half as the loss of product-definition authority. Intangible assets are written down when the cash flows behind them shrink. It is hard not to read the charge as an early, quiet acknowledgement of the September change.

**A tell in the working capital.** Days of payables outstanding is about 61 against 8 days of receivables and 7 days of inventory — a cash conversion cycle of minus 47 days. That is a supplier-financed model. It works beautifully at scale and reverses violently on the way down, which is exactly what the first quarter showed.

**A new voice, and what it is selling.** The 2026 initiative list — robotics, an internet-company car brand, a charging network with German luxury marques — is the vocabulary of a company that wants to be valued as a technology platform rather than an assembler. That ambition is not yet visible anywhere in the returns on capital.

---

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: DETERIORATING**, with a genuine restructuring underway that could change the label but has not yet.

Revenue is down 8%, gross margin down 4.7 points, the company has swung to a loss, operating cash flow ran minus CNY 12.38 billion in the half, and the brand is losing share inside an alliance that is growing. The Huawei handover is a real pivot and may prove to be the right one, but it is one week old and entirely unproven.

**The single thing the director must weigh before sizing this:** almost all of the apparent cheapness is a balance-sheet add-back, not an earnings discount. Value the whole company on revenue with no cash credit and the Hong Kong line trades at roughly 0.33x revenue against 0.65x for Li Auto and 0.55x for Leapmotor — a discount, but a defensible one for a brand losing relative share. Credit the CNY 30 billion of net cash and the operating business is being valued at almost nothing. The entire investment case turns on whether that cash is spare or is supplier float that a volume decline would consume. On the first quarter's evidence, it is a great deal more float than spare. Size the position to the version of the balance sheet you actually believe, not the version the company presents.

**Economic moat.** The moat here was never Seres's. It was Huawei's brand, Huawei's driving software and Huawei's retail network, rented to a manufacturer that supplied the factory. The type is best described as intangible-brand and channel access, held on loan. The evidence says it is narrowing on every measure the returns provide: gross margin from 29.1% in 2025 to 21.8% in the first half of 2026, return on invested capital down to 0.7%, pricing cut by CNY 50,000 on the entry trim, and the brand shrinking while its own alliance grew 26.5% through May. By the returns-and-margin test this is an eroding moat, not a wide one, and the 15 September transfer of channel and brand authority is the formal confirmation of that erosion rather than a cure for it.

**Terminal value.** The threat is real but not terminal. China's electric-vehicle market is growing, not shrinking, so this is not a melting base. The structural risk is different: in a vehicle built around someone else's driving software and sold through someone else's shops, the durable economics accrue to the software and channel owner, and the assembler is commoditised. Seres has partially hedged that — it owns 10% of Yinwang and it owns the AITO marks — but it has not escaped it. I judge the secular threat **material, not terminal**, and note that none of the eight named structural forces in our own controlled vocabulary describes this risk; forcing one on would be false precision.

**Fear-print or value trap?** Neither cleanly. It is a genuine de-rating from a genuinely absurd listing price, on top of a real margin shock, in a business whose competitive position got weaker in the same quarter. The cheapness is real on a revenue basis and overstated on a cash basis. That combination argues for patience and a small size, not for conviction in either direction.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a moat that is being eroded · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.

interrogator_dossier:
# Forensic Dossier — Seres Group Co., Ltd (9927.HK / 601127.SS)

**Date of review:** 2026-10-05 (continuing coverage; full prior review 2026-09-22) · **Price used:** HK$36.48 (Hong Kong listing 9927.HK, HKD, live quote 2026-10-05) · Figures in Chinese yuan (CNY) unless stated

**What changed since the last look (dated, 23 September to 5 October 2026).** Three facts are new, and they pull in opposite directions:

1. **30 September 2026 — a new five-year agreement with Huawei** (announced 1 October, reported by CnEVPost). The two companies will jointly set up a dedicated AITO team, Huawei keeps providing technology support, AITO stays inside Huawei's HIMA alliance (the Harmony Intelligent Mobility Alliance, Huawei's group of partner car brands), and Seres keeps the product, design, marketing, retail and service lead it took on 15 September. Financial terms were not disclosed. Under the previous model Huawei took roughly 10% per vehicle in technology and channel fees, and Seres's 2025 purchases from Huawei came to CNY 56.05 billion. This narrows the worst reading of the 15 September handover: Huawei is not walking away from the brand for at least five years. It does not answer the question that matters for value, which is what the new arrangement costs.
2. **30 September 2026 — refreshed AITO M8 opened pre-sales at CNY 389,800, CNY 30,000 above its predecessor's CNY 359,800 starting price**, after a CNY 1.5 billion upgrade programme. A price increase is the first pricing-power signal in 2026 after the CNY 50,000 cut to the M6 entry trim in June; it is partly paid for by more content (Huawei's latest driver-assistance system across the range), so it is not a clean like-for-like price rise.
3. **1 October 2026 — HIMA alliance September deliveries of 37,490 vehicles, down 29.15% year on year and 10.95% month on month**, the alliance's fourth straight year-on-year decline; year-to-date deliveries are still up 5.27% at 367,229. Trade press attributes part of the drop to model changeovers. Seres's own September figure was not available to me at the time of writing (my web-search budget for this session was exhausted; CnEVPost's September roundup does not break out Seres). For a business whose consensus needs a record-matching second half, an alliance down 29% in the last month of the third quarter is the wrong direction.

Net effect: one tail risk narrowed (partner exit), one small positive pricing signal, one near-term negative volume signal. None of it changes the assessment below, which is carried forward from the 22 September review with these facts added.

**A note on sources before anything else.** No earnings-call transcript exists for this company in our licensed data feed, and Chinese A-share issuers with a Hong Kong secondary listing do not hold the quarterly analyst calls that American companies do. There is therefore no multi-quarter transcript arc to read. Everything below is built from the company's own filed numbers (eight quarters of income statement, balance sheet and cash flow), its 12 July 2026 profit warning, its 19 August 2026 half-year report, and dated trade-press coverage of the Huawei partnership. Where I quote, I quote the filed half-year report as relayed by CnEVPost on 19 August 2026. I have invented nothing, and where a fact could not be verified I say so.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Seres makes the AITO (Wenjie) range of premium electric and range-extended sport-utility vehicles in Chongqing. It is not really an ordinary carmaker. Until one week ago it was the manufacturing half of a partnership in which Huawei did almost everything that touches the customer — defined the product, designed the vehicle, built the brand, and sold the cars through its own retail network — while Seres built them. That arrangement is what turned a loss-making minivan maker into a company with CNY 165 billion of revenue.

The arc across the last three years is one of the steepest in the industry, in both directions.

**2021 to 2023 — the pre-Huawei company.** Revenue of CNY 16.7 billion in 2021 rising to CNY 35.8 billion in 2023, with losses every year: CNY 1.82 billion, CNY 3.83 billion, CNY 2.45 billion. This was a subscale manufacturer going nowhere.

**2024 to 2025 — the Huawei years.** Revenue quadrupled to CNY 145.2 billion in 2024 and CNY 165.1 billion in 2025, and the company made money for the first time: CNY 5.95 billion and CNY 5.96 billion of net income. Gross margin reached 29.1% in 2025 — extraordinary for a volume carmaker and a direct product of Huawei's brand pricing power. Management spent heavily to secure the relationship: CNY 2.5 billion in July 2024 for the AITO trademarks and design patents, and CNY 11.5 billion in August 2024 for a 10% stake in Shenzhen Yinwang, Huawei's intelligent-automotive unit (the deal completed in September 2025). On 5 November 2025 the company listed in Hong Kong at HK$131.5 a share, raising roughly CNY 12.9 billion.

**2026 — the unwind.** The story since has contracted on every axis. First-half revenue fell 7.87% to CNY 57.49 billion, gross margin fell 4.7 percentage points to 21.8%, and the company swung to a net loss of CNY 1.72 billion from a CNY 2.94 billion profit a year earlier. In June the company cut the entry price of the new M6 by CNY 50,000, from CNY 279,800 to CNY 229,800 — an 18% cut on the trim that sets the brand's price floor. Then on 15 September 2026 Huawei handed operational control of AITO back to Seres: product definition, vehicle design, brand marketing, retail channels and service operations all transfer. AITO stays inside Huawei's HIMA alliance and keeps buying Huawei's driving software, but Seres must now build and fund its own sales network.

**What was quietly added.** While the core brand was shrinking, 2026 saw a remarkable burst of new initiatives: a premium-charging joint venture with BMW and Mercedes (17 April), a new vehicle brand connected to ByteDance (3 June), a second new brand called Aiva through affiliate Saidou (9 June), a humanoid robot (15 June), and a United Arab Emirates dealership (6 February). Five new directions in five months, from a company whose one profitable product line was losing share.

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

The company's explanation for the half-year loss is specific and testable. It blames input costs — battery-grade lithium carbonate up 132.2% year on year on an average daily price basis, plus "structural shortages and sharp price increases" in automotive-grade chips — and says it chose not to pass those costs to customers. It also took a CNY 1.75 billion write-down of intangible assets, attributed to "rapid technological iteration in the NEV industry."

| Management's claim | What the filed numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| The problem is input costs, not demand | Unit sales were 196,580, down only 1.02%; electric-vehicle units actually rose 3.87% to 178,777. Revenue fell 7.87%, so the average selling price fell about 7%. Gross margin fell 4.7 points. | **Largely supported.** Volume held; price and cost did the damage. This is genuinely a margin event, not a demand collapse. |
| "We declined to pass these costs to customers" | True in the sense that prices were not raised — but the company went the other way and *cut* the M6 entry price by CNY 50,000 in June. | **Poorer than the story.** This is not restraint; it is the absence of pricing power, described kindly. |
| Scale is still building | Half-year revenue of CNY 57.49 billion is below the CNY 62.40 billion of a year earlier; the second half of 2025 alone did CNY 102.6 billion. The business is running below its own recent peak. | **Diverges.** |
| The write-down reflects industry pace | The CNY 1.75 billion charge sits against CNY 12.3 billion of intangible assets carried on the balance sheet, much of it capitalised development spending. Writing off capitalised development because technology moved on is the textbook sign that the spending was capitalised too aggressively in the first place. | **Concerning.** The charge is honest; what it reveals about the earlier accounting is not flattering. |
| The balance sheet is a fortress — cash above CNY 73.15 billion, 57% of total assets, with interest-bearing debt only 3.2% of assets | Both figures are accurate. But the cash is funded by supplier credit: CNY 38.8 billion of notes payable to suppliers plus CNY 19.9 billion of trade payables. Net working capital is only CNY 3.84 billion. The company collects from customers in about 8 days and pays suppliers in about 61. | **Accurate but seriously misleading if read as spare cash.** See section 6. |

**The single most important forensic finding in this file** concerns that cash. In the first quarter of 2026, operating cash flow was *minus CNY 20.95 billion* in three months — the supplier float draining after the year-end volume push. The second quarter put CNY 8.47 billion back. Across the half, operating cash flow was minus CNY 12.38 billion. A cash balance that swings by twenty billion on working-capital timing is not a store of value the way an investor instinctively reads "57% of assets are cash." It is the float of a business that is paid instantly and pays late, and it shrinks when volumes shrink.

**Two numbers in our own screener file are wrong and must not be used.** The scan reports price-to-free-cash-flow of 2.0x and a discounted-cash-flow fair value of 198.1 — both computed from the 2025 peak-year cash flow. On a trailing twelve-month basis free cash flow is *minus* CNY 3.27 billion. The screener's net-debt field is also wrong; the corrected balance-sheet figure is in section 6.

---

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rating: Declining**, judged from disclosure behaviour rather than call transcripts, since none exist.

The sequence is telling. On **12 July 2026** the company issued a profit warning flagging a half-year net loss of CNY 1.5 billion to CNY 1.8 billion and naming the causes as rising material costs and asset write-downs. On **19 August 2026** it reported a loss of CNY 1.72 billion — inside its own range, and close to the middle of it. That is competent, unpanicked disclosure and it deserves credit.

But the *content* of the disclosure has shifted from offensive to defensive in one year. The 2025 language was about scale, premium positioning and a 29% gross margin. The 2026 language is about lithium prices, chip shortages, write-downs and "maintaining premium supply standards" — the vocabulary of a management team explaining a result rather than setting a direction. Research and development spending rose 27.4% to CNY 3.73 billion into a shrinking revenue base, which reads as commitment rather than retreat; but it sits alongside five new ventures launched in five months, which reads as a company casting about for the next story because the current one has stopped working.

---

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Score: Medium.**

The evidence that exists is good. The July warning was issued roughly five weeks before the result, gave a numerical range, named the causes, and the reported figure landed inside it. Chinese issuers are required to warn on large swings, so this is compliance rather than virtue — but plenty of companies warn late, warn vaguely, or warn low and then miss their own range. Seres did none of those.

Against that, the screener's earnings-beat record is 2 of the last 4 quarters, a 50% hit rate, which is coin-flip. And there is a structural pattern the director should hold in mind: this company's results are extremely back-half-weighted. The first half of 2025 was CNY 62.4 billion of revenue against CNY 102.6 billion in the second half. The same shape is embedded in the current consensus, which expects CNY 159.3 billion for full-year 2026 against CNY 57.5 billion delivered in the first half — implying a second half of roughly CNY 102 billion, essentially matching the prior year's record second half at a moment when the brand is losing share. That is a demanding number and it has not been de-risked.

---

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

With no calls, the pressure points must be inferred from what the company does and does not quantify. Three stand out.

**The Huawei dependency was never quantified, and now it is changing.** Seres has never disclosed what it pays Huawei — for the driving software, for the retail channel, for the brand. The 15 September restructuring changes all of those economics at once, and the company disclosed no new fee or equity arrangement alongside it. An investor is being asked to underwrite a transition whose cost is undisclosed.

**AITO's own volumes are not broken out.** The company reports total units. The alliance-level data that is public tells an uncomfortable story: Huawei's HIMA alliance delivered about 192,000 units from January to May 2026, up 26.5% year on year, while Seres's revenue fell 8% over the half. The alliance is growing; Seres's share of it is not. In August, HIMA deliveries themselves turned negative, down 5.52% year on year.

**Nobody has been made to explain the working-capital swing.** A negative CNY 20.95 billion operating quarter in a company that headlines its cash position is the question I would ask first, and there is no public forum in which it has been asked.

There is a further gap worth stating plainly: I could find no dated analyst price target for the Hong Kong line. Our data provider has no price-target coverage for this listing, and the web-search budget for this session was exhausted before a broker target could be sourced. I therefore use no target figure anywhere in this file.

---

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 **The cash is supplier float, not a war chest.** Cash and short-term investments of CNY 73.13 billion are financed by CNY 38.8 billion of supplier notes and CNY 19.9 billion of trade payables. Netting the supplier notes and the CNY 4.35 billion of genuine borrowings leaves roughly **CNY 30 billion of defensible net cash** — about CNY 17.2 a share, or HK$20.1. The company's own framing (debt is 3.2% of assets) implies nearly CNY 69 billion, which would be more than the entire Hong Kong-line market value. I do not accept that framing, and the first quarter's cash flow is the reason.

🔴 **Returns on capital have gone to nothing.** Trailing return on equity is 3.6% and return on invested capital 0.7%. The screener's full-year figures are worse still. A company earning less on its capital than it can earn on a bank deposit is not compounding.

🔴 **Capitalised development spending written off.** CNY 1.75 billion of intangibles impaired for "rapid technological iteration," against CNY 12.3 billion still carried. A further CNY 2.31 billion sits in "other gains and losses."

🔴 **The partner stepped back from this brand and only this brand.** Huawei retains operational leadership of the other four HIMA marques — Luxeed, Stelato, Maextro and Shangjie. It handed back the one it had built first. That ordering matters.

🔴 **Five new ventures in five months** while the core brand shrank: a charging joint venture, a ByteDance-linked brand, the Aiva brand, a humanoid robot, a Gulf dealership. Each is a call on management attention and capital.

🔴 **The listing itself was sold at a peak.** The November 2025 initial public offering priced at HK$131.5, valuing the whole company near CNY 196 billion on CNY 165 billion of revenue — roughly 1.2x revenue for a vehicle assembler, when the closest listed comparables trade around 0.55x to 0.65x. Much of the 73% decline since is the deflation of that price, not new information.

🟢 **Volume held.** Units fell only 1.02% and electric units rose 3.87%. The franchise did not lose its customers; it lost its price.

🟢 **The loss is smaller than it looks.** Strip the CNY 1.75 billion write-down and the half-year result is an operating stumble of a few percent on CNY 57.5 billion of revenue, not a structural cash loss.

🟢 **Seres now owns the customer.** Whatever the execution risk, product definition, design, brand and retail all move in-house from 15 September. The retail margin Huawei captured is now Seres's to capture — and Seres already owns the AITO trademarks outright.

🟢 **A real, under-recognised financial asset.** The 10% stake in Huawei's Yinwang unit, bought for CNY 11.5 billion and carried at about CNY 13.5 billion, is a minority interest in the supplier of driving software to the entire HIMA alliance and to third parties. It earns no line in the income statement that an investor would notice.

🟢 **Honest pre-announcement.** The July warning was specific, early and accurate.

---

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

**The language of the 15 September announcement is the signal.** Huawei transferred "product definition, product design, brand marketing, retail channels and service operations." That is not a delegation of tasks; it is the return of an entire commercial function. Read one way it is a promotion — Seres graduates from contract manufacturer to brand owner. Read the other way, the party that made the brand work has decided its time is better spent on four other brands, and the manufacturer now has to reproduce Huawei's retail machine from a standing start, with falling volumes, in a price war. Both readings are available from the same sentence. The second is the one the share price is pricing.

**The sequencing of the write-down.** The impairment of capitalised development landed in the same half as the loss of product-definition authority. Intangible assets are written down when the cash flows behind them shrink. It is hard not to read the charge as an early, quiet acknowledgement of the September change.

**A tell in the working capital.** Days of payables outstanding is about 61 against 8 days of receivables and 7 days of inventory — a cash conversion cycle of minus 47 days. That is a supplier-financed model. It works beautifully at scale and reverses violently on the way down, which is exactly what the first quarter showed.

**A new voice, and what it is selling.** The 2026 initiative list — robotics, an internet-company car brand, a charging network with German luxury marques — is the vocabulary of a company that wants to be valued as a technology platform rather than an assembler. That ambition is not yet visible anywhere in the returns on capital.

---

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: DETERIORATING**, with a genuine restructuring underway that could change the label but has not yet.

Revenue is down 8%, gross margin down 4.7 points, the company has swung to a loss, operating cash flow ran minus CNY 12.38 billion in the half, and the brand is losing share inside an alliance that is growing. The Huawei handover is a real pivot and may prove to be the right one, but it is one week old and entirely unproven.

**The single thing the director must weigh before sizing this:** almost all of the apparent cheapness is a balance-sheet add-back, not an earnings discount. Value the whole company on revenue with no cash credit and the Hong Kong line trades at roughly 0.33x revenue against 0.65x for Li Auto and 0.55x for Leapmotor — a discount, but a defensible one for a brand losing relative share. Credit the CNY 30 billion of net cash and the operating business is being valued at almost nothing. The entire investment case turns on whether that cash is spare or is supplier float that a volume decline would consume. On the first quarter's evidence, it is a great deal more float than spare. Size the position to the version of the balance sheet you actually believe, not the version the company presents.

**Economic moat.** The moat here was never Seres's. It was Huawei's brand, Huawei's driving software and Huawei's retail network, rented to a manufacturer that supplied the factory. The type is best described as intangible-brand and channel access, held on loan. The evidence says it is narrowing on every measure the returns provide: gross margin from 29.1% in 2025 to 21.8% in the first half of 2026, return on invested capital down to 0.7%, pricing cut by CNY 50,000 on the entry trim, and the brand shrinking while its own alliance grew 26.5% through May. By the returns-and-margin test this is an eroding moat, not a wide one, and the 15 September transfer of channel and brand authority is the formal confirmation of that erosion rather than a cure for it.

**Terminal value.** The threat is real but not terminal. China's electric-vehicle market is growing, not shrinking, so this is not a melting base. The structural risk is different: in a vehicle built around someone else's driving software and sold through someone else's shops, the durable economics accrue to the software and channel owner, and the assembler is commoditised. Seres has partially hedged that — it owns 10% of Yinwang and it owns the AITO marks — but it has not escaped it. I judge the secular threat **material, not terminal**, and note that none of the eight named structural forces in our own controlled vocabulary describes this risk; forcing one on would be false precision.

**Fear-print or value trap?** Neither cleanly. It is a genuine de-rating from a genuinely absurd listing price, on top of a real margin shock, in a business whose competitive position got weaker in the same quarter. The cheapness is real on a revenue basis and overstated on a cash basis. That combination argues for patience and a small size, not for conviction in either direction.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a moat that is being eroded · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.

Both figures are true and both are misleading. That cash is financed by CNY 38.8 billion of notes payable to suppliers and CNY 19.9 billion of trade payables. Net working capital is CNY 3.84 billion.
